```text
74	// applySorts sort an issues-related session based on the provided
75	// sortType string
76	func applySorts(sess db.Session, sortType string, priorityRepoID int64) {
77		// Since this sortType is dynamically created, it has to be treated specially.
78		if after, ok := strings.CutPrefix(sortType, ScopeSortPrefix); ok {
79			scope := after
80			sess.Join("LEFT", "issue_label", "issue.id = issue_label.issue_id")
81			// "exclusive_order=0" means "no order is set", so exclude it from the JOIN criteria and then "LEFT JOIN" result is also null
82			sess.Join("LEFT", "label", "label.id = issue_label.label_id AND label.exclusive_order <> 0 AND label.name LIKE ?", scope+"/%")
83			// Use COALESCE to make sure we sort NULL last regardless of backend DB (2147483647 == max int)
84			sess.OrderBy("COALESCE(label.exclusive_order, 2147483647) ASC").Desc("issue.id")
85			return
86		}
87
88		switch sortType {
89		case "oldest":
90			sess.Asc("issue.created_unix").Asc("issue.id")
91		case "recentupdate":
92			sess.Desc("issue.updated_unix").Desc("issue.created_unix").Desc("issue.id")
93		case "recentclose":
94			sess.Desc("issue.closed_unix").Desc("issue.created_unix").Desc("issue.id")
95		case "leastupdate":
96			sess.Asc("issue.updated_unix").Asc("issue.created_unix").Asc("issue.id")
97		case "mostcomment":
98			sess.Desc("issue.num_comments").Desc("issue.created_unix").Desc("issue.id")
99		case "leastcomment":
100			sess.Asc("issue.num_comments").Desc("issue.created_unix").Desc("issue.id")
101		case "priority":
102			sess.Desc("issue.priority").Desc("issue.created_unix").Desc("issue.id")
103		case "nearduedate":
104			// 253370764800 is 01/01/9999 @ 12:00am (UTC)
105			sess.Join("LEFT", "milestone", "issue.milestone_id = milestone.id").
106				OrderBy("CASE " +
107					"WHEN issue.deadline_unix = 0 AND (milestone.deadline_unix = 0 OR milestone.deadline_unix IS NULL) THEN 253370764800 " +
108					"WHEN milestone.deadline_unix = 0 OR milestone.deadline_unix IS NULL THEN issue.deadline_unix " +
109					"WHEN milestone.deadline_unix < issue.deadline_unix OR issue.deadline_unix = 0 THEN milestone.deadline_unix " +
110					"ELSE issue.deadline_unix END ASC").
111				Asc("issue.created_unix").
112				Asc("issue.id")
113		case "farduedate":
114			sess.Join("LEFT", "milestone", "issue.milestone_id = milestone.id").
115				OrderBy("CASE " +
116					"WHEN milestone.deadline_unix IS NULL THEN issue.deadline_unix " +
117					"WHEN milestone.deadline_unix < issue.deadline_unix OR issue.deadline_unix = 0 THEN milestone.deadline_unix " +
118					"ELSE issue.deadline_unix END DESC").
119				Desc("issue.created_unix").
120				Desc("issue.id")
121		case "priorityrepo":
122			sess.OrderBy("CASE "+
123				"WHEN issue.repo_id = ? THEN 1 "+
124				"ELSE 2 END ASC", priorityRepoID).
```

```text
82	// GetIssueStats returns issue statistic information by given conditions.
83	func GetIssueStats(ctx context.Context, opts *IssuesOptions) (*IssueStats, error) {
84		if len(opts.IssueIDs) <= MaxQueryParameters {
85			return getIssueStatsChunk(ctx, opts, opts.IssueIDs)
86		}
87
88		// If too long a list of IDs is provided, we get the statistics in
89		// smaller chunks and get accumulates. Note: this could potentially
90		// get us invalid results. The alternative is to insert the list of
91		// ids in a temporary table and join from them.
92		accum := &IssueStats{}
93		for i := 0; i < len(opts.IssueIDs); {
94			chunk := min(i+MaxQueryParameters, len(opts.IssueIDs))
95			stats, err := getIssueStatsChunk(ctx, opts, opts.IssueIDs[i:chunk])
96			if err != nil {
97				return nil, err
98			}
99			accum.OpenCount += stats.OpenCount
100			accum.ClosedCount += stats.ClosedCount
101			accum.YourRepositoriesCount += stats.YourRepositoriesCount
102			accum.AssignCount += stats.AssignCount
103			accum.CreateCount += stats.CreateCount
104			accum.MentionCount += stats.MentionCount
105			accum.ReviewRequestedCount += stats.ReviewRequestedCount
106			accum.ReviewedCount += stats.ReviewedCount
107			i = chunk
108		}
109		return accum, nil
110	}
111
112	func getIssueStatsChunk(ctx context.Context, opts *IssuesOptions, issueIDs []int64) (*IssueStats, error) {
113		stats := &IssueStats{}
114
115		sess := db.GetEngine(ctx).
116			Join("INNER", "repository", "`issue`.repo_id = `repository`.id")
117
118		var err error
119		stats.OpenCount, err = applyIssuesOptions(sess, opts, issueIDs).
120			And("issue.is_closed = ?", false).
121			Count(new(Issue))
122		if err != nil {
123			return stats, err
124		}
125		stats.ClosedCount, err = applyIssuesOptions(sess, opts, issueIDs).
126			And("issue.is_closed = ?", true).
127			Count(new(Issue))
128		return stats, err
129	}

136		}
137
138		if len(issueIDs) > 0 {
139			sess.In("issue.id", issueIDs)
140		}
141
142		applyLabelsCondition(sess, opts)
143
144		applyMilestoneCondition(sess, opts)
145
146		applyProjectCondition(sess, opts)
147
148		applyAssigneeCondition(sess, opts.AssigneeID)
149

151

155

158		}
159

162		}
163
164		if opts.IsPull.Has() {
```

```text
commit cf185ec66f344da943c76a9bfb4501f03ac45dc3
Author: Ethan Turner <citrusdeodorant@gmail.com>
Date:   Thu Sep 17 02:11:28 2026 -0400

    feat(issues): group the issue and pull request lists by label scope

    The pull request list is flat. You can filter it by label, but you cannot
    see the open pull requests split by the kind of change each one makes.

    Add a "Group by" dropdown listing the exclusive label scopes the repository
    has. Pick one and the list renders as a collapsible section per label in
    that scope, with a final "Uncategorized" section for the issues that carry
    no label in the scope. Collapsing uses details and summary, so it needs no
    JavaScript.

    This reuses Gitea's exclusive scoped labels, so it needs no new column and
    no migration. Attaching a second label in the same scope already removes
    the first, which is what makes one section per issue well defined.

    Two layers derive the groups and must agree. applyGroupByLabelScope orders
    the rows in SQL so the issues of one label sit together, and it runs before
    applySorts, so the chosen sort orders the issues inside each group.
    IssueList.GroupByExclusiveLabelScope then cuts the loaded page into groups.
    Both order the groups the same way: uncategorized last, then by
    exclusive_order with 0 treated as unset, then by label id. The tie-break is
    the label id and not the label name, because SQL collation does not match
    Go string comparison, and a group that spans two pages would then move.

    Mark the Kind/* labels in options/label/Advanced.yaml exclusive, so a
    repository created with that label set can group by Kind with no setup.

    The row markup moves from templates/shared/issuelist.tmpl into
    templates/shared/issuelist_items.tmpl, so a group can render its rows
    without repeating the pager. The dashboard, notification and milestone
    lists still call shared/issuelist and are unchanged.

    Group counts are the number shown on the current page, not the total across
    pages. A group that spans a page boundary repeats its heading on both.

    Closes #26

    Assisted-by: Claude Code:claude-opus-5
```

 `./models/issues/deadline_test.go`

```text
1	// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
2	// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
3
4	package issues_test
5
6	import (
7		"testing"
8		"time"
9
10		issues_model "gitea.dev/models/issues"
11		"gitea.dev/modules/timeutil"
12
13		"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
14	)
15
16	func TestIssueDeadlineStatus(t *testing.T) {
17		now := time.Date(2024, 1, 10, 12, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
18		defer timeutil.MockSet(now)()
19		nowTS := timeutil.TimeStamp(now.Unix())
20
21		cases := []struct {
22			name    string
23			issue   issues_model.Issue
24			overdue bool
25			nearDue bool
26		}{
27			{"no deadline", issues_model.Issue{}, false, false},
28			{"far future", issues_model.Issue{DeadlineUnix: nowTS.AddDuration(96 * time.Hour)}, false, false},
29			{"just outside window", issues_model.Issue{DeadlineUnix: nowTS.AddDuration(issues_model.NearDueDuration).Add(1)}, false, false},
30			{"exactly at window edge", issues_model.Issue{DeadlineUnix: nowTS.AddDuration(issues_model.NearDueDuration)}, false, true},
31			{"inside window", issues_model.Issue{DeadlineUnix: nowTS.AddDuration(time.Hour)}, false, true},
32			{"deadline is now", issues_model.Issue{DeadlineUnix: nowTS}, true, false},
33			{"overdue", issues_model.Issue{DeadlineUnix: nowTS.Add(-1)}, true, false},
34			{"closed before deadline", issues_model.Issue{IsClosed: true, ClosedUnix: nowTS.Add(-3600), DeadlineUnix: nowTS.AddDuration(time.Hour)}, false, false},
35			{"closed after deadline", issues_model.Issue{IsClosed: true, ClosedUnix: nowTS, DeadlineUnix: nowTS.Add(-3600)}, true, false},
36			{"closed, no deadline", issues_model.Issue{IsClosed: true, ClosedUnix: nowTS}, false, false},
37		}
38		for _, c := range cases {
39			t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
40				assert.Equal(t, c.overdue, c.issue.IsOverdue())
41				assert.Equal(t, c.nearDue, c.issue.IsNearDue())
42				assert.False(t, c.issue.IsOverdue() && c.issue.IsNearDue(), "overdue and near-due must be mutually exclusive")
43			})
44		}
45	}
46
47	func TestMilestoneDeadlineStatus(t *testing.T) {
48		now := time.Date(2024, 1, 10, 12, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
49		defer timeutil.MockSet(now)()
50		nowTS := timeutil.TimeStamp(now.Unix())
51
52		load := func(m *issues_model.Milestone) *issues_model.Milestone {
53			m.AfterLoad()
54			return m
55		}
56
57		noDeadline := load(&issues_model.Milestone{})
58		assert.False(t, noDeadline.IsOverdue)
59		assert.False(t, noDeadline.IsNearDue)
60		assert.Empty(t, noDeadline.DeadlineString)
61
62		soon := load(&issues_model.Milestone{DeadlineUnix: nowTS.AddDuration(time.Hour)})
63		assert.False(t, soon.IsOverdue)
64		assert.True(t, soon.IsNearDue)
65		assert.NotEmpty(t, soon.DeadlineString)
66
67		overdue := load(&issues_model.Milestone{DeadlineUnix: nowTS.Add(-1)})
68		assert.True(t, overdue.IsOverdue)
69		assert.False(t, overdue.IsNearDue)
70
71		far := load(&issues_model.Milestone{DeadlineUnix: nowTS.AddDuration(96 * time.Hour)})
72		assert.False(t, far.IsOverdue)
73		assert.False(t, far.IsNearDue)
74
75		closedInTime := load(&issues_model.Milestone{IsClosed: true, ClosedDateUnix: nowTS.Add(-3600), DeadlineUnix: nowTS.AddDuration(time.Hour)})
76		assert.False(t, closedInTime.IsOverdue)
77		assert.False(t, closedInTime.IsNearDue)
78
79		closedLate := load(&issues_model.Milestone{IsClosed: true, ClosedDateUnix: nowTS, DeadlineUnix: nowTS.Add(-3600)})
80		assert.True(t, closedLate.IsOverdue)
81		assert.False(t, closedLate.IsNearDue)
82
83		// NumOpenIssues is still computed as before.
84		m := load(&issues_model.Milestone{NumIssues: 5, NumClosedIssues: 2})
85		assert.Equal(t, 3, m.NumOpenIssues)
86	}
87
```

```text
18	func TestIssueList_GroupByExclusiveLabelScope(t *testing.T) {
19		kindBug := scopedTestLabel(1, "Kind/Bug", true, 1)
20		kindFeature := scopedTestLabel(2, "Kind/Feature", true, 2)
21		// the Advanced.yaml "Reviewed/Invalid" + "Reviewed/Won't Fix" case: same order, different labels
22		kindTiedHigh := scopedTestLabel(3, "Kind/Docs", true, 3)
23		kindTiedLow := scopedTestLabel(4, "Kind/Testing", true, 3)
24		kindUnordered := scopedTestLabel(5, "Kind/Chore", true, 0)
25		kindNotExclusive := scopedTestLabel(6, "Kind/Security", false, 1)
26		kindSubScope := scopedTestLabel(7, "Kind/UI/Bug", true, 1)
27		otherScope := scopedTestLabel(8, "Priority/High", true, 1)
28
29		issue := func(id int64, labels ...*issues_model.Label) *issues_model.Issue {
30			return &issues_model.Issue{ID: id, Labels: labels}
31		}
32		// group is described as its label ID (0 for the uncategorised group) plus the issue IDs in it
33		type wantGroup struct {
34			labelID  int64
35			issueIDs []int64
36		}
37
38		cases := []struct {
39			name   string
40			scope  string
41			issues issues_model.IssueList
42			want   []wantGroup
43		}{
44			{
45				name:  "empty list",
46				scope: "Kind",
47			},
48			{
49				name:   "empty scope collapses to a single uncategorised group",
50				scope:  "",
51				issues: issues_model.IssueList{issue(1, kindBug), issue(2)},
52				want:   []wantGroup{{labelID: 0, issueIDs: []int64{1, 2}}},
53			},
54			{
55				name:   "no issue carries a label in the scope",
56				scope:  "Kind",
57				issues: issues_model.IssueList{issue(1), issue(2, otherScope)},
58				want:   []wantGroup{{labelID: 0, issueIDs: []int64{1, 2}}},
59			},
60			{
61				name:   "ordered labels first, uncategorised last",
62				scope:  "Kind",
63				issues: issues_model.IssueList{issue(1), issue(2, kindFeature), issue(3, kindBug)},
64				want: []wantGroup{
65					{labelID: kindBug.ID, issueIDs: []int64{3}},
66					{labelID: kindFeature.ID, issueIDs: []int64{2}},
67					{labelID: 0, issueIDs: []int64{1}},
68				},
69			},
70			{
71				name:   "labels sharing an exclusive order tie-break on label ID",
72				scope:  "Kind",
73				issues: issues_model.IssueList{issue(1, kindTiedLow), issue(2, kindTiedHigh)},
74				want: []wantGroup{
75					{labelID: kindTiedHigh.ID, issueIDs: []int64{2}},
76					{labelID: kindTiedLow.ID, issueIDs: []int64{1}},
77				},
78			},
79			{
80				name:   "unordered label sorts after ordered ones but before uncategorised",
81				scope:  "Kind",
82				issues: issues_model.IssueList{issue(1, kindUnordered), issue(2), issue(3, kindFeature)},
83				want: []wantGroup{
84					{labelID: kindFeature.ID, issueIDs: []int64{3}},
85					{labelID: kindUnordered.ID, issueIDs: []int64{1}},
86					{labelID: 0, issueIDs: []int64{2}},
87				},
88			},
89			{
90				name:   "a non-exclusive label has no scope",
91				scope:  "Kind",
92				issues: issues_model.IssueList{issue(1, kindNotExclusive)},
93				want:   []wantGroup{{labelID: 0, issueIDs: []int64{1}}},
94			},

97				scope:  "Kind",

99				want:   []wantGroup{{labelID: 0, issueIDs: []int64{1}}},
100			},

105				want:   []wantGroup{{labelID: kindBug.ID, issueIDs: []int64{1}}},

111				want:   []wantGroup{{labelID: kindBug.ID, issueIDs: []int64{3, 1, 2}}},
112			},

115		for _, c := range cases {
```

```text
361	func buildIssueOverview(ctx *context.Context, unitType unit.Type) {
362		// ----------------------------------------------------
363		// Determine user; can be either user or organization.
364		// Return with NotFound or ServerError if unsuccessful.
365		// ----------------------------------------------------
366
367		ctxUser := prepareDashboardContextUserOrgTeams(ctx)
368		if ctx.Written() {
369			return
370		}
371
372		// Default to recently updated, unlike repository issues list
373		sortType := util.IfZero(ctx.FormString("sort"), "recentupdate")
374
375		// --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
376		// Distinguish User from Organization.
377		// Org:
378		// - Remember pre-determined viewType string for later. Will be posted to ctx.Data.
379		//   Organization does not have view type and filter mode.
380		// User:
381		// - Use ctx.FormString("type") to determine filterMode.
382		//  The type is set when clicking for example "assigned to me" on the overview page.
383		// - Remember either this or a fallback. Will be posted to ctx.Data.
384		// --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
385
386		// TODO: distinguish during routing
387
388		viewType := ctx.FormString("type")
389		var filterMode int
390		switch viewType {
391		case "assigned":
392			filterMode = issues_model.FilterModeAssign
393		case "created_by":
394			filterMode = issues_model.FilterModeCreate
395		case "mentioned":
396			filterMode = issues_model.FilterModeMention
397		case "review_requested":
398			filterMode = issues_model.FilterModeReviewRequested
399		case "reviewed_by":
400			filterMode = issues_model.FilterModeReviewed
401		case "your_repositories":
402			fallthrough
403		default:
404			filterMode = issues_model.FilterModeYourRepositories
405			viewType = "your_repositories"
406		}
407
408		isPullList := unitType == unit.TypePullRequests
409		opts := &issues_model.IssuesOptions{
410			IsPull:     optional.Some(isPullList),
411			SortType:   sortType,
412			IsArchived: optional.Some(false),
413			Doer:       ctx.Doer,
414		}
415		// --------------------------------------------------------------------------
416		// Build opts (IssuesOptions), which contains filter information.
417		// Will eventually be used to retrieve issues relevant for the overview page.
418		// Note: Non-final states of opts are used in-between, namely for:
419		//       - Keyword search
420		//       - Count Issues by repo
421		// --------------------------------------------------------------------------
422
423		// Get repository IDs where User/Org/Team has access.
424		if ctx.Org != nil && ctx.Org.Organization != nil {
425			opts.Owner = ctx.Org.Organization.AsUser()
426			opts.Team = ctx.Org.Team
427
428			issue.PrepareFilterIssueLabels(ctx, 0, ctx.Org.Organization.AsUser())
429			if ctx.Written() {
430				return
431			}
432		}
433		// Get filter by author id & assignee id
434		// the existing "/posters" handlers doesn't work for this case, it is unable to list the related users correctly.
435		// In the future, we need something like github: "author:user1" to accept usernames directly.
436		posterUsername := ctx.FormString("poster")
437		ctx.Data["FilterPosterUsername"] = posterUsername
438		opts.PosterID = user.GetFilterUserIDByName(ctx, posterUsername)
439		assigneeUsername := ctx.FormString("assignee")
440		ctx.Data["FilterAssigneeUsername"] = assigneeUsername
441		opts.AssigneeID = user.GetFilterUserIDByName(ctx, assigneeUsername)
442
443		searchMode := ctx.FormString("search_mode")
444
445		// Search all repositories which
446		//
447		// As user:
448		// - Owns the repository.
449		// - Have collaborator permissions in repository.
450		//
451		// As org:
452		// - Owns the repository.
453		//
454		// As team:
455		// - Team org's owns the repository.
456		// - Team has read permission to repository.
457		repoOpts := repo_model.SearchRepoOptions{
458			Actor:       ctx.Doer,
459			OwnerID:     ctxUser.ID,
460			Private:     true,
```

```text
// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package issues

import (
	"time"

	"gitea.dev/modules/timeutil"
)

// NearDueDuration is the window before a deadline in which an open issue, pull request
// or milestone counts as near due. Deadlines are pinned to 23:59:59 local time by
// routers/common/deadline.go, so in practice this covers the next three calendar days.
const NearDueDuration = 72 * time.Hour

// calcDeadlineStatus computes the overdue / near-due state shared by Issue and Milestone.
// The two are mutually exclusive: a passed deadline is overdue, never near due.
func calcDeadlineStatus(deadlineUnix timeutil.TimeStamp, isClosed bool, closedUnix timeutil.TimeStamp) (isOverdue, isNearDue bool) {
	if deadlineUnix == 0 {
		return false, false
	}
	if isClosed {
		return closedUnix >= deadlineUnix, false
	}
	now := timeutil.TimeStampNow()
	if now >= deadlineUnix {
		return true, false
	}
	return false, deadlineUnix <= now.AddDuration(NearDueDuration)
}
```

```text
// It omits the nil, false, zero int/int64 and empty string values,
// because they are default empty values for "ctx.FormXxx" calls.
// If 0 or false need to be included, use string values: "0" and "false".
// Build rules:
// * Even parameters: always build as query string: a=b&c=d
// * Odd parameters:
// * * {"/anything", param-pairs...} => "/?param-paris"
// * * {"anything?old-params", new-param-pairs...} => "anything?old-params&new-param-paris"
// * * Otherwise: {"old&params", new-param-pairs...} => "old&params&new-param-paris"
// * * Other behaviors are undefined yet.
func QueryBuild(a ...any) template.URL {
	var reqPath, s string
	hasTrailingSep := false
	if len(a)%2 == 1 {
		if v, ok := a[0].(string); ok {
			s = v
		} else if v, ok := a[0].(template.URL); ok {
			s = string(v)
		} else {
			panic("QueryBuild: invalid argument")
		}
		hasTrailingSep = s != "&" && strings.HasSuffix(s, "&")
		if strings.HasPrefix(s, "/") || strings.Contains(s, "?") {
			if s1, s2, ok := strings.Cut(s, "?"); ok {
				reqPath = s1 + "?"
				s = s2
			} else {
				reqPath += s + "?"
				s = ""
			}
		}
	}
	for i := len(a) % 2; i < len(a); i += 2 {
		k, ok := a[i].(string)
		if !ok {
			panic("QueryBuild: invalid argument")
		}
		var v string
		if va, ok := a[i+1].(string); ok {
			v = va
		} else if a[i+1] != nil {
			if !isQueryParamEmpty(a[i+1]) {
				v = fmt.Sprint(a[i+1])
			}
		}
		// pos1 to pos2 is the "k=v&" part, "&" is optional
		pos1 := strings.Index(s, "&"+k+"=")
		if pos1 != -1 {
			pos1++
		} else if strings.HasPrefix(s, k+"=") {
			pos1 = 0
		}
		pos2 := len(s)
		if pos1 == -1 {
			pos1 = len(s)
		} else {
			pos2 = pos1 + 1
			for pos2 < len(s) && s[pos2-1] != '&' {
				pos2++
			}
		}
		if v != "" {
			sep := ""
			hasPrefixSep := pos1 == 0 || (pos1 <= len(s) && s[pos1-1] == '&')
			if !hasPrefixSep {
				sep = "&"
			}
			s = s[:pos1] + sep + k + "=" + url.QueryEscape(v) + "&" + s[pos2:]
		} else {
			s = s[:pos1] + s[pos2:]
		}
	}
	if s != "" && s[len(s)-1] == '&' && !hasTrailingSep {
```

```text
460	// ones that can be grouped by. Sorting needs an exclusive order to mean anything, but grouping does
461	// not, so the two dropdowns are offered different sets.
462	func prepareIssueFilterLabelScopes(ctx *context.Context, allLabels []*issues_model.Label) []string {
463		groupableSet := make(map[string]bool)
464		orderedSet := make(map[string]bool)
465		for _, label := range allLabels {
466			scope := label.ExclusiveScope()
467			if len(scope) == 0 {
468				continue
469			}
470			groupableSet[scope] = true
471			if label.ExclusiveOrder > 0 {
472				orderedSet[scope] = true
473			}
474		}
475		orderedScopes := slices.Collect(maps.Keys(orderedSet))
476		sort.Strings(orderedScopes)
477		groupableScopes := slices.Collect(maps.Keys(groupableSet))
478		sort.Strings(groupableScopes)
479		ctx.Data["ExclusiveLabelScopes"] = orderedScopes
480		ctx.Data["GroupableLabelScopes"] = groupableScopes
481		return groupableScopes
482	}

484	// parseIssueGroupScope reads the "group" query parameter. An unknown scope silently turns grouping
485	// off rather than erroring, so a stale bookmark still renders the list.
486	func parseIssueGroupScope(ctx *context.Context, groupableScopes []string) string {
487		scope := ctx.FormString("group")
488		if !slices.Contains(groupableScopes, scope) {
489			return ""
490		}
491		return scope

801		ctx.Data["DefaultCloseReason"] = issues_model.DefaultCloseReason(isPullList)
802
803		projectIDs := parseProjectIDsFromQuery(ctx)
804
805		prepareIssueFilterAndList(ctx, ctx.FormInt64("milestone"), projectIDs, optional.Some(isPullList))

807			return
```

```text
const ScopeSortPrefix = "scope-"

// IssuesOptions represents options of an issue.
type IssuesOptions struct { //nolint:revive // export stutter
	Paginator          *db.ListOptions
	RepoIDs            []int64 // overwrites RepoCond if the length is not 0
	AllPublic          bool    // include also all public repositories
	RepoCond           builder.Cond
	AssigneeID         string // "(none)" or "(any)" or a user ID
	PosterID           string // "(none)" or "(any)" or a user ID
	MentionedID        int64
	ReviewRequestedID  int64
	ReviewedID         int64
	SubscriberID       int64
	MilestoneIDs       []int64
	ProjectIDs         []int64
	IsClosed           optional.Option[bool]
	IsPull             optional.Option[bool]
	LabelIDs           []int64
	IncludedLabelNames []string
	ExcludedLabelNames []string
	IncludeMilestones  []string
	SortType           string
	// GroupLabelScope orders rows so that issues sharing a label in this exclusive label scope
	// are contiguous, which is what lets a page be rendered as groups.
	GroupLabelScope   string
	IssueIDs          []int64
	UpdatedAfterUnix  int64
	UpdatedBeforeUnix int64
	// prioritize issues from this repo
	PriorityRepoID int64
	IsArchived     optional.Option[bool]
	Owner          *user_model.User   // issues permission scope, it could be an organization or a user
	Team           *organization.Team // issues permission scope
	Doer           *user_model.User   // issues permission scope
}

// Copy returns a copy of the options.
// Be careful, it's not a deep copy, so `IssuesOptions.RepoIDs = {...}` is OK while `IssuesOptions.RepoIDs[0] = ...` is not.
func (o *IssuesOptions) Copy(edit ...func(options *IssuesOptions)) *IssuesOptions {
	if o == nil {
		return nil
	}
	v := *o
	for _, e := range edit {
		e(&v)
	}
	return &v
}

// applySorts sort an issues-related session based on the provided

func applySorts(sess db.Session, sortType string, priorityRepoID int64) {

	if after, ok := strings.CutPrefix(sortType, ScopeSortPrefix); ok {
		scope := after
```

```text
// SearchIssues search issues by options.
func SearchIssues(ctx context.Context, opts *SearchOptions) ([]int64, int64, error) {
	ix := *globalIndexer.Load()

	if opts.Keyword == "" || opts.IsKeywordNumeric() {
		// This is a conservative shortcut.
		// If the keyword is empty or an integer, db has better (at least not worse) performance to filter issues.
		// When the keyword is empty, it tends to listing rather than searching issues.
		// So if the user creates an issue and list issues immediately, the issue may not be listed because the indexer needs time to index the issue.
		// Even worse, the external indexer like elastic search may not be available for a while,
		// and the user may not be able to list issues completely until it is available again.
		ix = db.GetIndexer()
	}

	result, err := ix.Search(ctx, opts)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, 0, err
	}
	return SearchResultToIDSlice(result), result.Total, nil
}

func SearchResultToIDSlice(result *internal.SearchResult) []int64 {
	ret := make([]int64, 0, len(result.Hits))
	for _, hit := range result.Hits {
		ret = append(ret, hit.ID)
	}
	return ret
}

// CountIssues counts issues by options. It is a shortcut of SearchIssues(ctx, opts) but only returns the total count.
func CountIssues(ctx context.Context, opts *SearchOptions) (int64, error) {
	opts = opts.Copy(func(options *SearchOptions) { options.Paginator = &db_model.ListOptions{PageSize: 0} })

	_, total, err := SearchIssues(ctx, opts)
	return total, err
}

func SupportedSearchModes() []indexer.SearchMode {
	gi := globalIndexer.Load()
	if gi == nil {
		return nil
	}
	return (*gi).SupportedSearchModes()
}
```

```text
	totalInt := int(min(total, int64(math.MaxInt)))

func (p *Pagination) WithUnlimitedPaging(curRows int, hasNext bool) *Pagination {
	p.Paginater.SetUnlimitedPaging(curRows, hasNext)
	return p
}

func (p *Pagination) AddParamFromQuery(q url.Values) {
	for key, values := range q {
		if key == "page" || len(values) == 0 || (len(values) == 1 && values[0] == "") {
			continue
		}
		for _, value := range values {
			urlParam := fmt.Sprintf("%s=%v", url.QueryEscape(key), url.QueryEscape(value))
			p.urlParams = append(p.urlParams, urlParam)
		}
	}
}

func (p *Pagination) AddParamFromRequest(req *http.Request) {
	p.AddParamFromQuery(req.URL.Query())
}
```

```text
func TestIndexer(t *testing.T, indexer internal.Indexer) {
	_, err := indexer.Init(t.Context())
	require.NoError(t, err)

	require.NoError(t, indexer.Ping(t.Context()))

	var (
		ids  []int64
		data = map[int64]*internal.IndexerData{}
	)
	{
		d := generateDefaultIndexerData()
		for _, v := range d {
			ids = append(ids, v.ID)
			data[v.ID] = v
		}
		require.NoError(t, indexer.Index(t.Context(), d...))
		waitData(t, indexer, int64(len(data)))
	}

	defer func() {
		require.NoError(t, indexer.Delete(t.Context(), ids...))
	}()

	for _, c := range cases {
		t.Run(c.Name, func(t *testing.T) {
			if len(c.ExtraData) > 0 {
				require.NoError(t, indexer.Index(t.Context(), c.ExtraData...))
				for _, v := range c.ExtraData {
					data[v.ID] = v
				}
				waitData(t, indexer, int64(len(data)))
				defer func() {
					for _, v := range c.ExtraData {
						require.NoError(t, indexer.Delete(t.Context(), v.ID))
						delete(data, v.ID)
					}
					waitData(t, indexer, int64(len(data)))
				}()
			}

			result, err := indexer.Search(t.Context(), c.SearchOptions)
			require.NoError(t, err)

			if c.Expected != nil {
				c.Expected(t, data, result)
			} else {
				ids := make([]int64, 0, len(result.Hits))
				for _, hit := range result.Hits {
					ids = append(ids, hit.ID)
				}
				assert.Equal(t, c.ExpectedIDs, ids)
				assert.Equal(t, c.ExpectedTotal, result.Total)
			}

			// test counting
			c.SearchOptions.Paginator = &db.ListOptions{PageSize: 0}
			countResult, err := indexer.Search(t.Context(), c.SearchOptions)
			require.NoError(t, err)
			assert.Empty(t, countResult.Hits)
			assert.Equal(t, result.Total, countResult.Total)
		})
	}
```
```text
}

// Search searches for issues
func (i *Indexer) Search(ctx context.Context, options *internal.SearchOptions) (*internal.SearchResult, error) {
	// FIXME: I tried to avoid importing models here, but it seems to be impossible.
	//        We can provide a function to register the search function, so models/issues can register it.
	//        So models/issues will import modules/indexer/issues, it's OK because it's by design.
	//        But modules/indexer/issues has already imported models/issues to do UpdateRepoIndexer and UpdateIssueIndexer.
	//        And to avoid circular import, we have to move the functions to another package.
	//        I believe it should be services/indexer, sounds great!
	//        But the two functions are used in modules/notification/indexer, that means we will import services/indexer in modules/notification/indexer.
	//        So that's the root problem:
	//        The notification is defined in modules, but it's using lots of things should be in services.

	cond := builder.NewCond()

	if options.Keyword != "" {
		repoCond := builder.In("repo_id", options.RepoIDs)
		if len(options.RepoIDs) == 1 {
			repoCond = builder.Eq{"repo_id": options.RepoIDs[0]}
		}
		subQuery := builder.Select("id").From("issue").Where(repoCond)
		searchMode := util.IfZero(options.SearchMode, i.SupportedSearchModes()[0].ModeValue)
		cond = builder.Or(
			buildMatchQuery(searchMode, "issue.name", options.Keyword),
			buildMatchQuery(searchMode, "issue.content", options.Keyword),
			builder.In("issue.id", builder.Select("issue_id").
				From("comment").
				Where(builder.And(
					builder.Eq{"type": issue_model.CommentTypeComment},
					builder.In("issue_id", subQuery),
					buildMatchQuery(searchMode, "content", options.Keyword),
				)),
			),
		)

		if options.IsKeywordNumeric() {
			cond = cond.Or(
				builder.Eq{"`index`": options.Keyword},
			)
		}
	}

	opt, err := ToDBOptions(ctx, options)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}

	// If pagesize == 0, return total count only. It's a special case for search count.
	if options.Paginator != nil && options.Paginator.PageSize == 0 {
		total, err := issue_model.CountIssues(ctx, opt, cond)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		return &internal.SearchResult{
			Total: total,
		}, nil
	}

	return i.FindWithIssueOptions(ctx, opt, cond)
}
```

```text
func applyLimit(sess db.Session, opts *IssuesOptions) {
	if opts.Paginator == nil || opts.Paginator.IsListAll() {
		return
	}

	start := 0
	if opts.Paginator.Page > 1 {
		start = (opts.Paginator.Page - 1) * opts.Paginator.PageSize
	}
	sess.Limit(opts.Paginator.PageSize, start)
}
```

```text
// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package integration

import (
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	issues_model "gitea.dev/models/issues"
	"gitea.dev/models/unittest"
	"gitea.dev/tests"

	"github.com/PuerkitoBio/goquery"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

// newExclusiveLabel creates an exclusive scoped label on user2/repo1 and returns its id.
func newExclusiveLabel(t *testing.T, sess *TestSession, name string, order int) int64 {
	t.Helper()
	req := NewRequestWithValues(t, "POST", "/user2/repo1/labels/new", map[string]string{
		"title":           name,
		"color":           "#112233",
		"exclusive":       "on",
		"exclusive_order": strconv.Itoa(order),
	})
	sess.MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusOK) // NewLabel answers with ctx.JSONRedirect
	label := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Label{RepoID: 1, Name: name})
	require.True(t, label.Exclusive, "%s must be exclusive, or its scope does not exist", name)
	return label.ID
}

func attachIssueLabel(t *testing.T, sess *TestSession, issueID, labelID int64) {
	t.Helper()
	req := NewRequestWithValues(t, "POST", fmt.Sprintf("/user2/repo1/issues/labels?issue_ids=%d", issueID), map[string]string{
		"action": "attach",
		"id":     strconv.FormatInt(labelID, 10),
	})
	sess.MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusOK)
}

// pullListGroups returns, per rendered group, its summary text and the issue indexes inside it.
func pullListGroups(t *testing.T, sess *TestSession, query string) (summaries []string, indexes [][]string) {
	t.Helper()
	req := NewRequest(t, "GET", "/user2/repo1/pulls?"+query)
	resp := sess.MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusOK)
	NewHTMLParser(t, resp.Body).doc.Find("details.issue-list-group").Each(func(_ int, group *goquery.Selection) {
		summaries = append(summaries, strings.Join(strings.Fields(group.Find("summary").Text()), " "))
		var groupIndexes []string
		group.Find(".item-body .index").Each(func(_ int, index *goquery.Selection) {
			groupIndexes = append(groupIndexes, strings.TrimSpace(index.Text()))
		})
		indexes = append(indexes, groupIndexes)
	})
	return summaries, indexes
}

// TestPullListGroupByLabelScope covers the "folder" view: ?group=<scope> renders the pull request
// list as one collapsible section per label in that exclusive scope, uncategorized last.
func TestPullListGroupByLabelScope(t *testing.T) {
	defer tests.PrepareTestEnv(t)()

	sess := loginUser(t, "user2")
	bugID := newExclusiveLabel(t, sess, "Kind/Bug", 1)
	featureID := newExclusiveLabel(t, sess, "Kind/Feature", 2)

	// repo1's open pull requests are #2, #3 and #5 (issue ids 2, 3 and 11)
	attachIssueLabel(t, sess, 3, bugID)     // #3
	attachIssueLabel(t, sess, 2, featureID) // #2
	// issue id 11 (#5) stays uncategorized

	t.Run("one group per label, uncategorized last", func(t *testing.T) {
		summaries, indexes := pullListGroups(t, sess, "group=Kind")
		require.Len(t, summaries, 3)
		assert.Contains(t, summaries[0], "Bug")
		assert.Contains(t, summaries[1], "Feature")
		assert.Contains(t, summaries[2], "Uncategorized")
		// exclusive order wins over the default newest-first ordering, which would put #5 first
		assert.Equal(t, [][]string{{"#3"}, {"#2"}, {"#5"}}, indexes)
	})

	t.Run("the group label is not repeated on every row in its group", func(t *testing.T) {
		req := NewRequest(t, "GET", "/user2/repo1/pulls?group=Kind")
		resp := sess.MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusOK)
		// issue 2 (#2) carries label1 and orglabel4 besides Kind/Feature
		feature := NewHTMLParser(t, resp.Body).doc.Find("details.issue-list-group").Eq(1)
		assert.NotContains(t, feature.Find(".labels-list").Text(), "Feature")
		assert.Equal(t, 2, feature.Find(".labels-list .item").Length(), "its other labels still show")
	})

	t.Run("the group by dropdown offers the scope", func(t *testing.T) {
		req := NewRequest(t, "GET", "/user2/repo1/pulls")
		resp := sess.MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusOK)
		assert.Positive(t, NewHTMLParser(t, resp.Body).doc.Find(`a[href*="group=Kind"]`).Length())
	})

	t.Run("an unknown scope falls back to the flat list", func(t *testing.T) {
		req := NewRequest(t, "GET", "/user2/repo1/pulls?group=NotAScope")
		resp := sess.MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusOK)
		htmlDoc := NewHTMLParser(t, resp.Body)
		assert.Equal(t, 0, htmlDoc.doc.Find("details.issue-list-group").Length())
		assert.Equal(t, 3, htmlDoc.doc.Find("#issue-list .item-body .index").Length())
	})

	t.Run("sort orders issues within a group", func(t *testing.T) {
		attachIssueLabel(t, sess, 11, bugID) // #5 joins the Kind/Bug folder

		_, indexes := pullListGroups(t, sess, "group=Kind&sort=oldest")
		assert.Equal(t, [][]string{{"#3", "#5"}, {"#2"}}, indexes)

		_, indexes = pullListGroups(t, sess, "group=Kind&sort=latest")
		assert.Equal(t, [][]string{{"#5", "#3"}, {"#2"}}, indexes)
	})
}
```

```text
func (i *Indexer) Init(_ context.Context) (bool, error) {
	if i == nil {
		return false, errors.New("cannot init nil indexer")
	}

	if i.Client != nil {
		return false, errors.New("indexer is already initialized")
	}

	i.Client = meilisearch.New(i.url, meilisearch.WithAPIKey(i.apiKey))
	_, err := i.Client.GetIndex(i.VersionedIndexName())
	if err == nil {
		return true, nil
	}
	_, err = i.Client.CreateIndex(&meilisearch.IndexConfig{
		Uid:        i.VersionedIndexName(),
		PrimaryKey: "id",
	})
	if err != nil {
		return false, err
	}

	i.checkOldIndexes()

	_, err = i.Client.Index(i.VersionedIndexName()).UpdateSettings(i.settings)
	return false, err
}
```

```text
    13	func ParseDeadlineDateToEndOfDay(date string) (timeutil.TimeStamp, error) {
    14		if date == "" {
    15			return 0, nil
    16		}
    17		deadline, err := time.ParseInLocation("2006-01-02", date, setting.DefaultUILocation)
    18		if err != nil {
    19			return 0, err
    20		}
    21		deadline = time.Date(deadline.Year(), deadline.Month(), deadline.Day(), 23, 59, 59, 0, deadline.Location())
    22		return timeutil.TimeStamp(deadline.Unix()), nil
    23	}
    24
    25	func ParseAPIDeadlineToEndOfDay(t *time.Time) (timeutil.TimeStamp, error) {
    26		if t == nil || t.IsZero() || t.Unix() == 0 {
    27			return 0, nil
    28		}
    29		deadline := time.Date(t.Year(), t.Month(), t.Day(), 23, 59, 59, 0, setting.DefaultUILocation)
    30		return timeutil.TimeStamp(deadline.Unix()), nil
    31	}
```

```text
     1	// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
     2	// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
     3
     4	package issues
     5
     6	import (
     7		"time"
     8
     9		"gitea.dev/modules/timeutil"
    10	)
    11
    12	// NearDueDuration is the window before a deadline in which an open issue, pull request
    13	// or milestone counts as near due. Deadlines are pinned to 23:59:59 local time by
    14	// routers/common/deadline.go, so in practice this covers the next three calendar days.
    15	const NearDueDuration = 72 * time.Hour
    16
    17	// calcDeadlineStatus computes the overdue / near-due state shared by Issue and Milestone.
    18	// The two are mutually exclusive: a passed deadline is overdue, never near due.
    19	func calcDeadlineStatus(deadlineUnix timeutil.TimeStamp, isClosed bool, closedUnix timeutil.TimeStamp) (isOverdue, isNearDue bool) {
    20		if deadlineUnix == 0 {
    21			return false, false
    22		}
    23		if isClosed {
    24			return closedUnix >= deadlineUnix, false
    25		}
    26		now := timeutil.TimeStampNow()
    27		if now >= deadlineUnix {
    28			return true, false
    29		}
    30		return false, deadlineUnix <= now.AddDuration(NearDueDuration)
    31	}
	}
	return nil
}

// IsOverdue checks if the issue is overdue
func (issue *Issue) IsOverdue() bool {
	isOverdue, _ := calcDeadlineStatus(issue.DeadlineUnix, issue.IsClosed, issue.ClosedUnix)
	return isOverdue
}

// IsNearDue checks if the issue's deadline is approaching but has not passed
func (issue *Issue) IsNearDue() bool {
	_, isNearDue := calcDeadlineStatus(issue.DeadlineUnix, issue.IsClosed, issue.ClosedUnix)
	return isNearDue
}
```

```text
// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package issues

import (
	"time"

	"gitea.dev/modules/timeutil"
)

// NearDueDuration is the window before a deadline in which an open issue, pull request
// or milestone counts as near due. Deadlines are pinned to 23:59:59 local time by
// routers/common/deadline.go, so in practice this covers the next three calendar days.
const NearDueDuration = 72 * time.Hour

// calcDeadlineStatus computes the overdue / near-due state shared by Issue and Milestone.
// The two are mutually exclusive: a passed deadline is overdue, never near due.
)

// DefaultUILocation is the location on the UI, so that we can display the time on UI.
var DefaultUILocation = time.Local

func loadTimeFrom(rootCfg ConfigProvider) {
	zone := rootCfg.Section("time").Key("DEFAULT_UI_LOCATION").String()
	if zone != "" {
		var err error
		DefaultUILocation, err = time.LoadLocation(zone)
		if err != nil {
			log.Fatal("Load time zone failed: %v", err)
		}
	}
	if DefaultUILocation == nil {
		DefaultUILocation = time.Local
	}
}
	timeZeroUnix = time.Time{}.Unix()
)

// MockSet sets the time to a mocked time.Time
func MockSet(now time.Time) func() {
	mockNow = now
	return MockUnset
}

// MockUnset will unset the mocked time.Time
func MockUnset() {
	mockNow = time.Time{}
}

// TimeStampNow returns now int64
func TimeStampNow() TimeStamp {
	if !mockNow.IsZero() {
		return TimeStamp(mockNow.Unix())
	}
	return TimeStamp(time.Now().Unix())
}

// Add adds seconds and return sum
func (ts TimeStamp) Add(seconds int64) TimeStamp {
	return ts + TimeStamp(seconds)
}

// AddDuration adds time.Duration and return sum
func (ts TimeStamp) AddDuration(interval time.Duration) TimeStamp {
	return ts + TimeStamp(interval/time.Second)
}

// Year returns the time's year
func (ts TimeStamp) Year() int {
	return ts.AsTime().Year()
}

// AsTime convert timestamp as time.Time in Local locale
func (ts TimeStamp) AsTime() (tm time.Time) {
	return ts.AsTimeInLocation(setting.DefaultUILocation)
}

// AsLocalTime convert timestamp as time.Time in local location
func (ts TimeStamp) AsLocalTime() time.Time {
	return time.Unix(int64(ts), 0)
}

// AsTimeInLocation convert timestamp as time.Time in Local locale
func (ts TimeStamp) AsTimeInLocation(loc *time.Location) time.Time {
	return time.Unix(int64(ts), 0).In(loc)
}
```

```text
export function initGlobalDropdown() {
  // do not init "custom" dropdowns, "custom" dropdowns are managed by their own code.
  registerGlobalSelectorFunc('.ui.dropdown:not(.custom)', (el) => {
    const $dropdown = fomanticQuery(el);
    if ($dropdown.data('module-dropdown')) return; // do not re-init if other code has already initialized it.

    $dropdown.dropdown('setting', {hideDividers: 'empty'});

    if (el.classList.contains('jump')) {
      // The "jump" means this dropdown is mainly used for "menu" purpose,
      // clicking an item will jump to somewhere else or trigger an action/function.
      // When a dropdown is used for non-refresh actions with tippy,
      // it must have this "jump" class to hide the tippy when dropdown is closed.
      $dropdown.dropdown('setting', {
        action: 'hide',
        onShow() {
          // hide associated tooltip while dropdown is open
```

````text
# Testing

Gitea has four kinds of automated tests: backend unit tests, integration tests,
end-to-end (e2e) tests, and migration tests. Local runs default to SQLite, so no
extra services are required to get started.

For prerequisites see [build-setup.md](build-setup.md); for the build workflow see
[development.md](development.md).

## Unit tests

Backend unit tests live in `*_test.go` files next to the code they cover. Set
`GITEA_TEST_LOG_SQL=1` to log all SQL statements executed during the tests.

```bash
make test-backend
```

To run a single backend test, use `go test` directly or the `#` selector:

```bash
go test -run '^TestName$' ./modulepath/
make test-backend#TestName
```

Frontend unit tests run with [Vitest](https://vitest.dev/):

```bash
make test-frontend
# single file:
pnpm exec vitest <path-filter>
```

## Integration tests

Integration tests exercise Gitea against a real database. They live in
`tests/integration/` and require [Git LFS](https://git-lfs.com/) to be installed.
The database is selected with `GITEA_TEST_DATABASE`; an empty value defaults to
SQLite, which needs no external service:

```bash
make test-integration
```

Run a single integration test with the `#` selector:

```bash
make test-integration#TestName
```

If you hit errors such as a mismatched database version or SSH push failures, try a
clean rebuild first:

```bash
make clean build
```

### Running against other databases

Set `GITEA_TEST_DATABASE` together with the matching `TEST_*` connection variables.
The commands below start a throwaway database container (press `Ctrl-C` to stop and
remove it) and then run the tests against it.

#### MySQL

```bash
docker run -e "MYSQL_DATABASE=test" -e "MYSQL_ALLOW_EMPTY_PASSWORD=yes" -p 3306:3306 --rm --name mysql mysql:latest
```

```bash
GITEA_TEST_DATABASE=mysql TEST_MYSQL_HOST=localhost:3306 TEST_MYSQL_DBNAME=test TEST_MYSQL_USERNAME=root TEST_MYSQL_PASSWORD='' make test-integration
```

#### PostgreSQL

PostgreSQL tests also use a MinIO container for object storage:

```bash
docker run -e "POSTGRES_DB=test" -e "POSTGRES_USER=postgres" -e "POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres" -p 5432:5432 --rm --name pgsql postgres:latest
docker run --rm -p 9000:9000 -e MINIO_ROOT_USER=123456 -e MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD=[REDACTED:generic-password] --name minio bitnamilegacy/minio:2023.8.31
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
)

func TestHeatmapEndpoints(t *testing.T) {
	defer tests.PrepareTestEnv(t)()

	// Mock time so fixture actions fall within the heatmap's time window
	timeutil.MockSet(time.Date(2021, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC))
	defer timeutil.MockUnset()

	session := loginUser(t, "user2")

	t.Run("UserProfile", func(t *testing.T) {
		defer tests.PrintCurrentTest(t)()
		req := NewRequest(t, "GET", "/user2/-/heatmap")
		resp := session.MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusOK)

		result := DecodeJSON(t, resp, map[string]any{})
		assert.Contains(t, result, "heatmapData")
		assert.Contains(t, result, "totalContributions")
		assert.Positive(t, result["totalContributions"])
	})

	t.Run("OrgDashboard", func(t *testing.T) {
		defer tests.PrintCurrentTest(t)()
		req := NewRequest(t, "GET", "/org/org3/dashboard/-/heatmap")
		resp := session.MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusOK)

		result := DecodeJSON(t, resp, map[string]any{})
		assert.Contains(t, result, "heatmapData")
		assert.Contains(t, result, "totalContributions")
	})

package common

import (
	"time"

	"gitea.dev/modules/setting"
	"gitea.dev/modules/timeutil"
)

func ParseDeadlineDateToEndOfDay(date string) (timeutil.TimeStamp, error) {
	if date == "" {
		return 0, nil
	}
	deadline, err := time.ParseInLocation("2006-01-02", date, setting.DefaultUILocation)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, err
	}
	deadline = time.Date(deadline.Year(), deadline.Month(), deadline.Day(), 23, 59, 59, 0, deadline.Location())
	return timeutil.TimeStamp(deadline.Unix()), nil
}

func ParseAPIDeadlineToEndOfDay(t *time.Time) (timeutil.TimeStamp, error) {
	if t == nil || t.IsZero() || t.Unix() == 0 {
		return 0, nil
	}
	deadline := time.Date(t.Year(), t.Month(), t.Day(), 23, 59, 59, 0, setting.DefaultUILocation)
	return timeutil.TimeStamp(deadline.Unix()), nil
````
```text
}

func TestCorrectIssueStats(t *testing.T) {
	assert.NoError(t, unittest.PrepareTestDatabase())

	// Because the condition is to have chunked database look-ups,
	// We have to more issues than `maxQueryParameters`, we will insert.
	// maxQueryParameters + 10 issues into the testDatabase.
	// Each new issues will have a constant description "Bugs are nasty"
	// Which will be used later on.
	defer test.MockVariableValue(&issues_model.MaxQueryParameters, 25)()
	issueAmount := issues_model.MaxQueryParameters + 10

	for i := range issueAmount {
		testInsertIssue(t, fmt.Sprintf("Issue %d", i+1), "Bugs are nasty", 0)
	}

	// Now we will get all issueID's that match the "Bugs are nasty" query.
	issues, err := issues_model.Issues(t.Context(), &issues_model.IssuesOptions{
		Paginator: &db.ListOptions{
			PageSize: issueAmount,
		},
		RepoIDs: []int64{1},
	})
	total := int64(len(issues))
	var ids []int64
	for _, issue := range issues {
		if issue.Content == "Bugs are nasty" {
			ids = append(ids, issue.ID)
		}
	}

	// Just to be sure.
	assert.NoError(t, err)
	assert.EqualValues(t, issueAmount, total)

	// Now we will call the GetIssueStats with these IDs and if working,
	// get the correct stats back.
	issueStats, err := issues_model.GetIssueStats(t.Context(), &issues_model.IssuesOptions{
		RepoIDs:  []int64{1},
		IssueIDs: ids,
	})

	// Now check the values.
	assert.NoError(t, err)
	assert.EqualValues(t, issueStats.OpenCount, issueAmount)
}
```

```text
func generateIssueIndexMapping() (mapping.IndexMapping, error) {
	mapping := bleve.NewIndexMapping()
	docMapping := bleve.NewDocumentMapping()

	numericFieldMapping := bleve.NewNumericFieldMapping()
	numericFieldMapping.Store = false
	numericFieldMapping.IncludeInAll = false
	docMapping.AddFieldMappingsAt("repo_id", numericFieldMapping)

	textFieldMapping := bleve.NewTextFieldMapping()
	textFieldMapping.Store = false
	textFieldMapping.IncludeInAll = false

	boolFieldMapping := bleve.NewBooleanFieldMapping()
	boolFieldMapping.Store = false
	boolFieldMapping.IncludeInAll = false

	numberFieldMapping := bleve.NewNumericFieldMapping()
	numberFieldMapping.Store = false
	numberFieldMapping.IncludeInAll = false

	docMapping.AddFieldMappingsAt("is_public", boolFieldMapping)

	docMapping.AddFieldMappingsAt("title", textFieldMapping)
}
```

```text
// UpdateIssueDeadline updates an issue deadline and adds comments. Setting a deadline to 0 means deleting it.
func UpdateIssueDeadline(ctx context.Context, issue *Issue, deadlineUnix timeutil.TimeStamp, doer *user_model.User) (err error) {
	// if the deadline hasn't changed do nothing
	if issue.DeadlineUnix == deadlineUnix {
		return nil
	}

	return db.WithTx(ctx, func(ctx context.Context) error {
		// Update the deadline
		if err = UpdateIssueCols(ctx, &Issue{ID: issue.ID, DeadlineUnix: deadlineUnix}, "deadline_unix"); err != nil {
			return err
		}

		// Make the comment
		if _, err = createDeadlineComment(ctx, doer, issue, deadlineUnix); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("createRemovedDueDateComment: %w", err)
		}
		return nil
	})
}
```

```text
var (
	// mockNow is NOT concurrency-safe!!
	mockNow time.Time

	// Used for IsZero, to check if timestamp is the zero time instant.
	timeZeroUnix = time.Time{}.Unix()
)

// MockSet sets the time to a mocked time.Time
func MockSet(now time.Time) func() {
	mockNow = now
	return MockUnset
}

// MockUnset will unset the mocked time.Time
func MockUnset() {
	mockNow = time.Time{}
}

// TimeStampNow returns now int64
func TimeStampNow() TimeStamp {
	if !mockNow.IsZero() {
		return TimeStamp(mockNow.Unix())
	}
	return TimeStamp(time.Now().Unix())
}

// Add adds seconds and return sum
func (ts TimeStamp) Add(seconds int64) TimeStamp {
	return ts + TimeStamp(seconds)
}
```

The dropdowns are plain server-rendered links. A new `due` param has to be added by hand in four template places (listed under Q2), and only pagination carries it along automatically. The `group` commit (cf185ec66f) touched exactly those spots.

## 1. How a simple dropdown is built (`templates/repo/issue/filter_list.tmpl`)

**Shared base link.** Line 3 builds one `$queryLink` holding every current filter value:
```
{{$queryLink := QueryBuild "?" "q" $.Keyword "type" $.ViewType "sort" $.SortType "state" $.State "labels" $.SelectLabels "milestone" $.MilestoneID "project" $projectIDsQuery "assignee" $.AssigneeID "poster" $.PosterUsername "archived_labels" (Iif $.ShowArchivedLabels "true") "group" $.GroupByLabelScope}}
```
- Each option's link is `QueryBuild $queryLink "<key>" <value>`, which replaces that one key and keeps the rest.
- Passing `NIL` (or `""`, `0`, `false`) removes the key. That is how an "any" option should work.
- `QueryBuild` lives in `modules/templates/helper.go:210`. Its doc comment at lines ~200-209 says empty values are dropped and `"?old&..."` gets merged.
- The values come from `ctx.Data` (`SortType`, `GroupByLabelScope`, …), not from reading the request in the template. A new `$.DueFilter` (or similar) has to be set in the handler.

**The "Group by" dropdown (lines 99-113)** is the closest model:
```
<div class="item ui dropdown jump">
  <span class="text">{{ctx.Locale.Tr "repo.issues.group_by"}}</span>
  {{svg "octicon-triangle-down" 14 "dropdown icon"}}
  <div class="menu">
    <a class="{{if not $.GroupByLabelScope}}active {{end}}item" href="{{QueryBuild $queryLink "group" NIL}}">…group_by.none…</a>
    {{range $scope := .GroupableLabelScopes}}
      <a class="{{if eq $.GroupByLabelScope $scope}}active {{end}}item" href="{{QueryBuild $queryLink "group" $scope}}">{{$scope}}</a>
```

**The Sort dropdown (lines 115-139)** follows the same pattern with fixed options, e.g. line 128:
```
<a class="{{if eq .SortType "nearduedate"}}active {{end}}item" href="{{QueryBuild $queryLink "sort" "nearduedate"}}">…
```
The active item is marked with an `active ` class prefix, and the default option checks `(not .SortType)`. The Type dropdown (lines 80-97) is the same shape but sits inside `{{if .IsSigned}}`.

**`filter_actions.tmpl` is not relevant.** It is the bulk-action toolbar for checked issues (`data-url="{{$.Link}}/milestone"` etc.) and contains no filter links.

- `filter_project` / `_all` / `_none` (1483-1485)
- `filter_assignee` / `_no_assignee` / `_any_assignee` (1486-1488)

- `repo.issues.due_date_not_set` "No due date set." (1712)
- `repo.milestones.no_due_date` "No due date" (1962)
- The form and error keys are at 1700-1718.

There is no key for "has a due date", "due today", "due this week" or a dropdown "any" option.

## 5. The near-due/overdue badge

- **Rows:** `templates/shared/issuelist_items.tmpl:109-120` (moved there from `shared/issuelist.tmpl` by cf185ec66f):
  ```
  {{if ne .DeadlineUnix 0}}
    {{if .IsOverdue}} …"tw-text-red"… "repo.issues.due_date_overdue"
    {{else if .IsNearDue}} …"tw-text-warning-text"… "repo.issues.due_date_near"
    <span class="due-date flex-text-inline {{$dueClass}}" …>{{svg "octicon-calendar" 14}}{{DateUtils.AbsoluteShort .DeadlineUnix}}
  ```
- **Methods:** `models/issues/issue.go:141` `IsOverdue()` and `:147` `IsNearDue()`. Both call `calcDeadlineStatus` in `models/issues/deadline.go:19-31`:
  - a closed issue is overdue if `closedUnix >= deadline`, and is never near due;
  - an open issue is overdue if `now >= deadline`;
  - an open issue is near due if `deadline <= now + NearDueDuration`.
  - `NearDueDuration = 72 * time.Hour` (`deadline.go:15`). Deadlines are pinned to 23:59:59 by `routers/common/deadline.go`.
  - Your SQL "overdue" / "due soon" filters should use the same constant and the same open/closed rules.
- **Other uses:** the same badge pattern is in `templates/repo/issue/sidebar/due_date.tmpl:7-13`, `milestone_issues.tmpl:40-43` and `milestones.tmpl:61-64`.
- **Existing due-date SQL:** the `nearduedate`/`farduedate` sorts in `models/issues/issue_search.go:107-118` combine the issue deadline with the milestone deadline. Decide whether your filter does the same.

## 6. Frontend JS

No JS hook is needed. A plain `<div class="item ui dropdown jump">` with `<a href>` items works with no extra code:
- `web_src/js/features/common-page.ts:59-70` (`initGlobalDropdown`) initialises every `.ui.dropdown:not(.custom)`. The `jump` class only sets `action: 'hide'` and tooltip handling.
- `web_src/js/features/repo-issue.ts:26-94` reads `labels` and `archived_labels` from the URL, but only for `.label-filter`.
- `web_src/js/features/repo-issue-list.ts:240-250` handles checkboxes, `.user-remote-search` (whose jump URL comes from the server-side `$queryLink`) and pin sorting. It also toggles `#issue-filters` / `#issue-actions` visibility when issues are checked (:35-38). Your dropdown sits inside `#issue-filters`, so it hides during bulk selection like the others.

**Test precedent:** `tests/integration/issue_group_by_scope_test.go:98` asserts `a[href*="group=Kind"]` to check that links carry the param.

_**Agent - sidechain (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-06 22:27:54Z)**_

Short answers: the new filter won't reach the counts by itself. Repo-page counts use a separate condition builder from the list. The dashboard and org pages filter only through `issue_indexer.SearchOptions`, so every backend needs it. Meilisearch would also need `deadline_unix` made filterable and its index version bumped. And changing an issue's deadline never reindexes the issue, so the external indexers can hold old deadline values.

## 1. `models/issues/issue_search.go` and `issue_stats.go`

- **`IssuesOptions` struct** (`issue_search.go:27-59`): Paginator, RepoIDs, AllPublic, RepoCond, AssigneeID/PosterID (strings), MentionedID, ReviewRequestedID, ReviewedID, SubscriberID, MilestoneIDs, ProjectIDs, IsClosed/IsPull (`optional.Option[bool]`), LabelIDs, IncludedLabelNames, ExcludedLabelNames, IncludeMilestones, SortType, GroupLabelScope, IssueIDs, `UpdatedAfterUnix`/`UpdatedBeforeUnix int64` (lines 51-52), PriorityRepoID, IsArchived, Owner, Team, Doer.
- **`applyConditions`** (`issue_search.go:256-314`) is what the list and `CountIssues` use. The updated-time filter is at lines 288-293:
  ```go
  if opts.UpdatedAfterUnix != 0 { sess.And(builder.Gte{"issue.updated_unix": opts.UpdatedAfterUnix}) }
  if opts.UpdatedBeforeUnix != 0 { sess.And(builder.Lte{"issue.updated_unix": opts.UpdatedBeforeUnix}) }
  ```
- **Due-date sorts** (`applySorts`, lines 103-120): both LEFT JOIN `milestone` and sort by the earlier of the issue and milestone deadlines.
  - `nearduedate` (106-110) pushes "no deadline" to the end by mapping it to 253370764800 (year 9999).
  - `farduedate` (115-118) has no zero guard. In DESC order, zeros fall to the end anyway. One quirk: if the milestone exists with deadline 0 and the issue has a deadline, the `milestone.deadline_unix < issue.deadline_unix` branch picks the milestone's 0.
  - There is no `deadline_unix != 0` WHERE guard anywhere in `models/issues`. The only zero checks are these CASE expressions and `calcDeadlineStatus` (`models/issues/deadline.go:20`).
  - You need to decide whether the filter looks only at `issue.deadline_unix` or also at the milestone deadline, as the sorts do.
- **`GetIssueStats` does not use `applyConditions`.** It calls `getIssueStatsChunk` (`issue_stats.go:112-129`), which uses its own `applyIssuesOptions` (lines 131-169).
  - That function applies only: RepoIDs, issueIDs, labels, milestone, project, assignee, poster, mentioned, review-requested, reviewed, IsPull.
  - It ignores UpdatedAfter/Before, SubscriberID, IsArchived, RepoCond, AllPublic, Owner/Doer/Team.
  - So a new field must also be added to `applyIssuesOptions`, or the repo-page open/closed counts won't change.
- **`GetIssueTotalTrackedTime`** (`models/issues/tracked_time.go:325`, chunk function at 345-352) also uses `applyIssuesOptions`. Adding the field there changes stats and tracked time together.
- `CountIssues` and `CountIssuesByRepo` (`issue_stats.go:43-80`) use `applyConditions`.

## 2. Indexer option mapping

**`modules/indexer/issues/dboptions.go` `ToSearchOptions`:**
- Copies Keyword, RepoIDs, AllPublic, IsPull, IsClosed, IsArchived (lines 20-27).
- Splits LabelIDs into NoLabelOnly / IncludedLabelIDs / ExcludedLabelIDs (29-41).
- Milestone: `NoConditionID` becomes `[0]` (43-47). Project: becomes NoProjectOnly (49-53).
- AssigneeID and PosterID are copied directly. Mention/Reviewed/ReviewRequested/Subscriber go through `convertID` to `optional` (55-72).
- UpdatedAfter/Before are copied only if `> 0` (74-79).
- SortType maps to SortBy (83-109); `priority`, `priorityrepo` and project sorting fall back to UpdatedDesc.
- It drops RepoCond, IncludedLabelNames/ExcludedLabelNames, IncludeMilestones, GroupLabelScope, PriorityRepoID, Owner/Team/Doer. It panics in dev/test if IssueIDs is set (17-19).

**Paginator:** it sets nothing special, just `searchOpt.Paginator = opts.Paginator` (line 81).
- For the repo keyword search, `statsOpts` (`routers/web/repo/issue_list.go:562-577`) has no Paginator, so it is nil.
- `ParsePaginator` (`modules/indexer/internal/paginator.go:21-25`) treats nil as "unlimited":
  - bleve: `MaxInt32`
  - meilisearch: capped at `maxTotalHits = 10000`
  - elasticsearch: capped at `maxPageSize`
  - db: `applyLimit` (`issue_search.go:157-159`) applies no limit
- `PageSize: 0` means count only. `CountIssues` sets it (`indexer.go:315`).

**`modules/indexer/issues/db/options.go` `ToDBOptions`** (lines 19-116) is the reverse:
- SortBy maps back to a SortType string; the default is `"newest"`.
- `convertID`: None becomes 0, and `Some(0)` becomes `NoConditionID`.
- `UpdatedAfterUnix: options.UpdatedAfterUnix.Value()`, i.e. 0 when unset.
- RepoCond, Owner, Team and Doer are set to nil explicitly.
- Milestone `[0]` becomes `NoConditionID`; NoLabelOnly becomes `LabelIDs=[0]`; IncludedAnyLabelIDs is turned into IncludedLabelNames.

**db indexer `Search`** (`modules/indexer/issues/db/db.go:67-126`): when PageSize is 0 it calls `issue_model.CountIssues` (which uses `applyConditions`); otherwise `FindWithIssueOptions`, then `IssueIDs` (also `applyConditions`). So dashboard counts on the db backend do go through `applyConditions`.

## 3. User dashboard and org issues/pulls

- **Routes:** `routers/web/web.go:554` (`/issues`), `:558` (`/pulls`), `:961-964` (org `/issues`, `/issues/{team}`, `/pulls`, `/pulls/{team}`). All go to `buildIssueOverview` (`routers/web/user/home.go:361-643`).
- **List:** `issue_indexer.SearchIssues(ctx, issue_indexer.ToSearchOptions(keyword, opts).Copy(...))` at `home.go:541`, then `GetIssuesByIDs`.
- **Counts:** `getUserIssueStats` (`home.go:771-848`) makes 8 `issue_indexer.CountIssues` calls on copies of `SearchOptions`. Any new `SearchOptions` field is carried through those copies automatically.
- **Which backend runs:** `SearchIssues` (`modules/indexer/issues/indexer.go:285-303`) uses the db indexer when the keyword is empty or numeric, and the configured backend otherwise.
- **So yes, the filter must go through the whole chain:**
  1. a new `IssuesOptions` field
  2. `ToSearchOptions`
  3. a new `internal.SearchOptions` field (`modules/indexer/issues/internal/model.go:80-118`)
  4. `ToDBOptions`
  5. `applyConditions`
  6. bleve, meilisearch and elasticsearch `Search`, for keyword searches
- **Template:** `templates/user/dashboard/issues.tmpl` has its own filter UI and does **not** include `repo/issue/filter_list.tmpl`.
  - It reuses only the partials `repo/issue/filter_item_label` (line 67) and `filter_item_user_fetch` (72-91), and has its own sort dropdown (93-104).
  - The `due` param would need adding to `$queryLink` (line 7), `$queryLinkWithFilter` (line 39) and the search form's hidden inputs (53-55).
- **Repo side, for comparison:** `templates/repo/issue/filter_list.tmpl:3` builds `$queryLink`, and `templates/repo/issue/search.tmpl:3-12` has the hidden inputs.

- `ParseDeadlineDateToEndOfDay(date string)` (lines 13-23) parses `"2006-01-02"` with `time.ParseInLocation(..., setting.DefaultUILocation)` and pins the result to 23:59:59 that day.

  ```go

  if opts.UpdatedBeforeUnix != 0 { sess.And(builder.Lte{"issue.updated_unix": opts.UpdatedBeforeUnix}) }
  ```

  - `nearduedate` (106-110) pushes "no deadline" to the end by mapping it to 253370764800 (year 9999).
  - `farduedate` (115-118) has no zero guard. In DESC order, zeros fall to the end anyway. One quirk: if the milestone exists with deadline 0 and the issue has a deadline, the `milestone.deadline_unix &lt; issue.deadline_unix` branch picks the milestone's 0.
  - There is no `deadline_unix != 0` WHERE guard anywhere in `models/issues`. The only zero checks are these CASE expressions and `calcDeadlineStatus` (`models/issues/deadline.go:20`).
  - You need to decide whether the filter looks only at `issue.deadline_unix` or also at the milestone deadline, as the sorts do.
- **`GetIssueStats` does not use `applyConditions`.** It calls `getIssueStatsChunk` (`issue_stats.go:112-129`), which uses its own `applyIssuesOptions` (lines 131-169).
  - That function applies only: RepoIDs, issueIDs, labels, milestone, project, assignee, poster, mentioned, review-requested, reviewed, IsPull.
  - It ignores UpdatedAfter/Before, SubscriberID, IsArchived, RepoCond, AllPublic, Owner/Doer/Team.
  - So a new field must also be added to `applyIssuesOptions`, or the repo-page open/closed counts won't change.

```text
func applyConditions(sess db.Session, opts *IssuesOptions) {
	if len(opts.IssueIDs) > 0 {
		sess.In("issue.id", opts.IssueIDs)
	}

	applyRepoConditions(sess, opts)

	if opts.IsClosed.Has() {
		sess.And("issue.is_closed=?", opts.IsClosed.Value())
	}

	applyAssigneeCondition(sess, opts.AssigneeID)
	applyPosterCondition(sess, opts.PosterID)

	if opts.MentionedID > 0 {
		applyMentionedCondition(sess, opts.MentionedID)
	}

	if opts.ReviewRequestedID > 0 {
		applyReviewRequestedCondition(sess, opts.ReviewRequestedID)
	}

	if opts.ReviewedID > 0 {
		applyReviewedCondition(sess, opts.ReviewedID)
	}

	if opts.SubscriberID > 0 {
		applySubscribedCondition(sess, opts.SubscriberID)
	}

	applyMilestoneCondition(sess, opts)

	if opts.UpdatedAfterUnix != 0 {
		sess.And(builder.Gte{"issue.updated_unix": opts.UpdatedAfterUnix})
	}
	if opts.UpdatedBeforeUnix != 0 {
		sess.And(builder.Lte{"issue.updated_unix": opts.UpdatedBeforeUnix})
	}

	applyProjectCondition(sess, opts)

	if opts.IsPull.Has() {
		sess.And("issue.is_pull=?", opts.IsPull.Value())
	}

	if opts.IsArchived.Has() {
		sess.And(builder.Eq{"repository.is_archived": opts.IsArchived.Value()})
	}

	applyLabelsCondition(sess, opts)

	if opts.Owner != nil {
		sess.And(repo_model.UserOwnedRepoCond(opts.Owner.ID))

		sess.And(issuePullAccessibleRepoCond("issue.repo_id", opts.Doer.ID, opts.Owner, opts.Team, opts.IsPull.Value()))
	}
}

func getIssueStatsChunk(ctx context.Context, opts *IssuesOptions, issueIDs []int64) (*IssueStats, error) {
	stats := &IssueStats{}

	sess := db.GetEngine(ctx).
		Join("INNER", "repository", "`issue`.repo_id = `repository`.id")

	var err error
	stats.OpenCount, err = applyIssuesOptions(sess, opts, issueIDs).
		And("issue.is_closed = ?", false).
		Count(new(Issue))
	if err != nil {
		return stats, err
	}
	stats.ClosedCount, err = applyIssuesOptions(sess, opts, issueIDs).
		And("issue.is_closed = ?", true).
		Count(new(Issue))
	return stats, err
}

func applyIssuesOptions(sess db.Session, opts *IssuesOptions, issueIDs []int64) db.Session {
	if len(opts.RepoIDs) > 1 {
		sess.In("issue.repo_id", opts.RepoIDs)
	} else if len(opts.RepoIDs) == 1 {
		sess.And("issue.repo_id = ?", opts.RepoIDs[0])
	}

	if len(issueIDs) > 0 {
		sess.In("issue.id", issueIDs)
	}

	applyLabelsCondition(sess, opts)

	applyMilestoneCondition(sess, opts)

	applyProjectCondition(sess, opts)

	applyAssigneeCondition(sess, opts.AssigneeID)

	applyPosterCondition(sess, opts.PosterID)

	if opts.MentionedID > 0 {
		applyMentionedCondition(sess, opts.MentionedID)
	}

	if opts.ReviewRequestedID > 0 {
		applyReviewRequestedCondition(sess, opts.ReviewRequestedID)
	}

	if opts.ReviewedID > 0 {
		applyReviewedCondition(sess, opts.ReviewedID)
	}

	if opts.IsPull.Has() {
		sess.And("issue.is_pull=?", opts.IsPull.Value())
	}

	return sess
}
```

```text
func TestIssueDueDateHighlight(t *testing.T) {
	defer tests.PrepareTestEnv(t)()

	issue := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: 10})
	repo := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &repo_model.Repository{ID: issue.RepoID})
	owner := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &user_model.User{ID: repo.OwnerID})

	session := loginUser(t, owner.Name)
	deadlineURL := fmt.Sprintf("/%s/%s/issues/%d/deadline", owner.Name, repo.Name, issue.Index)
	issueURL := fmt.Sprintf("/%s/%s/issues/%d", owner.Name, repo.Name, issue.Index)

	setDeadlineAndGetDueDate := func(t *testing.T, deadline string) *goquery.Selection {
		req := NewRequestWithValues(t, "POST", deadlineURL, map[string]string{"deadline": deadline})
		session.MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusOK)

		req = NewRequest(t, "GET", issueURL)
		resp := session.MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusOK)
		return NewHTMLParser(t, resp.Body).Find(".due-date")
	}

	t.Run("near due", func(t *testing.T) {
		tomorrow := time.Now().AddDate(0, 0, 1).Format("2006-01-02")
		dueDate := setDeadlineAndGetDueDate(t, tomorrow)
		assert.True(t, dueDate.HasClass("tw-text-warning-text"))
		assert.False(t, dueDate.HasClass("tw-text-red"))
		tooltip, _ := dueDate.Attr("data-tooltip-content")
		assert.Equal(t, "Due soon", tooltip)
	})

	t.Run("overdue", func(t *testing.T) {
		yesterday := time.Now().AddDate(0, 0, -1).Format("2006-01-02")
		dueDate := setDeadlineAndGetDueDate(t, yesterday)
		assert.True(t, dueDate.HasClass("tw-text-red"))
		assert.False(t, dueDate.HasClass("tw-text-warning-text"))
		tooltip, _ := dueDate.Attr("data-tooltip-content")
		assert.Equal(t, "Overdue", tooltip)
	})

	t.Run("far future", func(t *testing.T) {
		nextMonth := time.Now().AddDate(0, 1, 0).Format("2006-01-02")
		dueDate := setDeadlineAndGetDueDate(t, nextMonth)
		assert.False(t, dueDate.HasClass("tw-text-red"))
		assert.False(t, dueDate.HasClass("tw-text-warning-text"))
	})

	// leave the issue without a deadline for other tests relying on fixture state
	req := NewRequestWithValues(t, "POST", deadlineURL, map[string]string{"deadline": ""})
	session.MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusOK)
}
```

**Which pages should the Due date filter cover in this PR? (Oct 8 deadline is two days out.)**

Options:
- **Repo lists only (Recommended)** - Repo Issues + Pull Requests lists, plus the single-milestone issue page for free (it shares the same handler and template). Dashboard /issues, /pulls and org pages go to a follow-up issue. All filtering stays in SQL; ~8 files.
- **Also user/org dashboards** - Adds /issues, /pulls and org issue pages. Those filter only through the issue indexer, so the filter must be added to SearchOptions and implemented in db, bleve, elasticsearch and meilisearch (meilisearch also needs deadline_unix made filterable + an index version bump). Deadline edits also don't reindex today, so keyword searches could see stale deadlines. Realistically Large, not Medium.

**What should "Due this week" mean? Gitea has no week-start setting.**

Options:
- **Calendar week Mon–Sun (Recommended)** - Deadlines from Monday 00:00 to Sunday 23:59:59 of the current week, in the server's UI timezone (ISO 8601 week). Matches the label literally; includes earlier days this week, so items that went overdue on Monday still show. Clearly different from "Due soon" (rolling 72h).
- **Rolling next 7 days** - From the start of today through the end of today+6. Always looks a full week ahead, no week-start ambiguity, but overlaps heavily with "Due soon" and the label would read "Due in the next 7 days".
- **Calendar week Sun–Sat** - Same as the first option but starting Sunday (US convention).

**You're on the GitHub-generated branch `34-sort-issues-and-pull-requests-by-due-date` (no commits yet, same as main). The course convention is `feat/issue-<N>-...`. Which branch should the work go on?**

- **Keep current branch** - Work on `34-sort-issues-and-pull-requests-by-due-date` as-is.

**The issue proposes DeadlineBeforeUnix / DeadlineAfterUnix / HasDeadline range fields, and also says the filter and the #3 badge must never disagree. For CLOSED issues the badge uses different rules (Overdue = closed after its deadline; never Due soon). Which semantics?**

Options:
- **Pure deadline ranges (Recommended)** - Follow the proposed fields exactly: Overdue = deadline passed, Due soon = deadline within NearDueDuration, regardless of open/closed. Identical to the badge on the Open tab (the default view). On Closed/All tabs a closed-on-time issue with a past deadline still matches Overdue. Works in every indexer backend, so the dashboard behaves the same as the repo list.
- **Mirror the badge for closed too** - Overdue matches closed issues only if closed after the deadline; Due soon never matches closed issues. Exact badge agreement everywhere, but needs a closed_unix vs deadline_unix comparison that bleve/meilisearch/elasticsearch can't do (closed_unix isn't even indexed), so dashboard keyword searches would need extra index fields.

**Changing an issue's due date never re-indexes it today, so on the dashboard a keyword search combined with ?due= would filter on stale deadlines in bleve (the default indexer). How should I handle that?**

Options:
- **Re-index on deadline change (Recommended)** - Small fix needed for the dashboard filter to be correct: after a deadline is saved (web + API call sites), queue the issue for re-indexing. Not named in the issue, but without it a requested feature returns wrong results.
- **Leave it, document it** - Don't touch deadline saving; note the limitation in the PR and open a follow-up bug issue.


**Answer:** Repo + dashboard, incl. org (Recommended), Pure deadline ranges (Recommended), Re-index on deadline change (Recommended)

```text
<!-- markdownlint-disable MD029 -->
<!-- Rules are numbered continuously 1-15 across the sections below; check.sh error

# Maintenance rules

Five people maintain one shared set of docs. These rules exist so the set stays *one* set. Read
them before editing anything in `.claude-students/`. Rules marked **[checked]** are enforced by
`./.claude-students/check.sh`.

## Scope discipline

1. **Upstream wins.** `AGENTS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `docs/guidelines-*.md` are authoritative.
   Docs here summarise them and link to them; they never restate a rule differently and never
   contradict one. A contradiction is a bug in this folder, not in the project.
2. **One fact, one home.** Every fact lives in exactly one doc — the one whose `scope:` owns that
   path. Everywhere else, link to it. Duplicated facts are how five maintainers end up with five
   different answers.
3. **Durability test.** Record a fact only if it (a) took more than one discovery step to find and
   (b) will still be true after the next upstream merge. A one-off workaround, a sprint detail or
   anything about your own task fails this test — that belongs in `ai-logs/`.
4. **No process notes.** No TODOs, no open questions, no first person, no student names, no dates
   other than `verified-at`. This is a map of the code, not a journal.

## Form

5. **Template only [checked].** Use the `## ` headings from `_TEMPLATE.md`, all of them, in that
   order, with nothing added. If a section has nothing to say, write one line saying so.
6. **120-line cap [checked].** Going over means the scope is too broad. Split the doc, and add the
   new `INDEX.md` row in the same commit. `INDEX.md` itself is capped at 60 lines.
7. **Cite or delete [checked, partially].** Every claim names a repo path. A claim with no path is
   unverifiable by the next reader — delete it.
8. **Symbols, not line numbers [checked].** Write `models/db/context.go` → `WithTx`, never
   `models/db/context.go:143`. Line numbers rot at the next upstream merge and a stale number is
   worse than no number. Code fences stay at 10 lines or fewer — point at the file instead of
   copying it.
9. **Repo-relative paths [checked].** `models/db/context.go`, never `/home/you/gitea/models/...`.
10. **Whitespace [checked].** No trailing whitespace, LF endings, final newline — same as the rest
    of the repo (`.editorconfig`).

## Change control

11. **One universal set.** These docs live on `main` and nowhere else. Never keep a personal copy,
    a per-student folder, or a long-lived branch of them.
12. **Changes land by PR**, titled `docs(context): <subject>` per `AGENTS.md` Conventional Commits,
    with an `Assisted-by: AGENT_NAME:MODEL_VERSION` trailer and no `Co-Authored-By` or
    `Signed-off-by`.
13. **Fix in place.** If you discover while working that a doc is wrong or incomplete, correct it
    in the *same* PR as your code change and update `verified-at` to the commit you checked
    against. Leaving a doc stale for someone else to hit is the exact failure this folder exists to
    prevent. This rule applies to AI sessions too.
14. **New docs need three things in one commit [checked]:** the file, its `INDEX.md` row, and a
    `scope:` that does not overlap any existing doc's. If the scope overlaps, you wanted to edit
    that doc, not add one.
15. **`./.claude-students/check.sh` passes before you push [checked].** It is dependency-free and
    finishes in under a second.

## The guide layer (rules 16-22)

`guide/` holds a plain-English page for each reference page in `docs/`, same filename. It exists so
```

````markdown
# Plan: Issue #34 — filter issues and pull requests by due date

## Context

Gitea can sort by due date but not filter by it. Issue #34 asks for a **Due date** dropdown with these options: any, overdue, due today, due this week, due soon, has a due date, no due date. The selection goes in the URL as `?due=…` and combines with the existing filters.

The filter must:
- reuse `issues_model.NearDueDuration` (#3's badge window, `models/issues/deadline.go`);
- guard against `deadline_unix = 0`, the stored value for "no deadline";
- compute relative options on the server, using the same clock as the badge.

Jack owns the issue in the Sprint 1 milestone, and everything is due **Oct 8**.

**Decisions confirmed with you**

- **Pages:** repo Issues, repo Pull Requests, dashboard `/issues`, dashboard `/pulls`. The org view (`/org/X/issues|pulls`) is the same handler and template, so it gets the dropdown too.
- **Not on the milestone page:** the single-milestone issue page shares the repo handler and template, so it is gated out explicitly.
- **Semantics:** pure deadline ranges, using the fields the issue proposes: `DeadlineAfterUnix`, `DeadlineBeforeUnix`, `HasDeadline`. They match the badge exactly on the Open tab. On the Closed and All tabs, a closed issue matches by deadline alone.
- **"This week":** the calendar week, Monday 00:00 to Sunday 23:59:59, in `setting.DefaultUILocation`.
- **Re-index on deadline change:** saving a deadline will re-index the issue. Without this, dashboard keyword search combined with `?due=` filters on stale bleve data.
- **Branch:** `feat/issue-34-filter-by-due-date`, created from an up-to-date `main`. I won't touch the auto-generated `34-sort-…` branch.

**Option → bounds.** "now" is `timeutil.TimeStampNow().AsTime()`, the badge's clock, in `DefaultUILocation`. Bounds are inclusive.

| `due=` | After | Before | HasDeadline |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| *(absent / unknown)* | – | – | – |
| `overdue` | – | now | true |
| `today` | today 00:00 | today 23:59:59 | true |
| `week` | Mon 00:00 | Sun 23:59:59 | true |
| `soon` | now+1 | now + `NearDueDuration` | true |
| `set` | – | – | true |
| `none` | – | – | false |

Both bounds of `overdue` and `soon` are exactly the comparisons in `calcDeadlineStatus`. Setting any bound also forces `deadline_unix != 0`, at the model and indexer level, so even a caller that forgets `HasDeadline` cannot match undated rows.
````
