````text
## Approved Plan:
# Plan: Issue #34 — filter issues and pull requests by due date

## Context

Gitea can sort by due date but not filter by it. Issue #34 asks for a **Due date** dropdown with these options: any, overdue, due today, due this week, due soon, has a due date, no due date. The selection goes in the URL as `?due=…` and combines with the existing filters.

The filter must:
- reuse `issues_model.NearDueDuration` (#3's badge window, `models/issues/deadline.go`);
- guard against `deadline_unix = 0`, the stored value for "no deadline";
- compute relative options on the server, using the same clock as the badge.

Jack owns the issue in the Sprint 1 milestone, and everything is due **Oct 8**.

**Decisions confirmed with you**

- **Pages:** repo Issues, repo Pull Requests, dashboard `/issues`, dashboard `/pulls`. The org view (`/org/X/issues|pulls`) is the same handler and template, so it gets the dropdown too.
- **Not on the milestone page:** the single-milestone issue page shares the repo handler and template, so it is gated out explicitly.
- **Semantics:** pure deadline ranges, using the fields the issue proposes: `DeadlineAfterUnix`, `DeadlineBeforeUnix`, `HasDeadline`. They match the badge exactly on the Open tab. On the Closed and All tabs, a closed issue matches by deadline alone.
- **"This week":** the calendar week, Monday 00:00 to Sunday 23:59:59, in `setting.DefaultUILocation`.
- **Re-index on deadline change:** saving a deadline will re-index the issue. Without this, dashboard keyword search combined with `?due=` filters on stale bleve data.
- **Branch:** `feat/issue-34-filter-by-due-date`, created from an up-to-date `main`. I won't touch the auto-generated `34-sort-…` branch.

**Option → bounds.** "now" is `timeutil.TimeStampNow().AsTime()`, the badge's clock, in `DefaultUILocation`. Bounds are inclusive.

| `due=` | After | Before | HasDeadline |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| *(absent / unknown)* | – | – | – |
| `overdue` | – | now | true |
| `today` | today 00:00 | today 23:59:59 | true |
| `week` | Mon 00:00 | Sun 23:59:59 | true |
| `soon` | now+1 | now + `NearDueDuration` | true |
| `set` | – | – | true |
| `none` | – | – | false |

Both bounds of `overdue` and `soon` are exactly the comparisons in `calcDeadlineStatus`. Setting any bound also forces `deadline_unix != 0`, at the model and indexer level, so even a caller that forgets `HasDeadline` cannot match undated rows.
````

```markdown
Suggested new title: Filter issues and pull requests by due date

## User Story
As a maintainer running a sprint, I want to filter the issue and pull request lists down to what is overdue, due today, due this week or due soon so that I can triage deadline risk without reading every row.

## User Scenario
A maintainer opens the Issues tab of a repository with 400 open issues. Next to the Labels, Milestones, Projects, Poster and Assignee dropdowns there is a new **Due date** dropdown. They pick **Overdue**. The list now shows only the six issues whose due date has passed, each with its red "Overdue" badge, and the Open/Closed counts above the list say 6 / 0. The URL now ends in `?due=overdue`, so they paste it into the team chat. Later they switch to **Due this week** to plan the next few days, then type a keyword into the search box: the due-date filter stays applied. The same dropdown is on their dashboard Issues and Pull Requests pages (`/issues`, `/pulls`), so they can do the same across all of their repositories.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given a repository's Issues or Pull Requests list, or the dashboard Issues or Pull Requests page (including its organization view), when the page loads, then a **Due date** dropdown is shown with the options All due dates, Overdue, Due today, Due this week, Due soon, Has a due date and No due date. The single-milestone issue page does not show it.
- [ ] AC2: Given issues with past, future and no due dates, when **Overdue** (`?due=overdue`) is selected, then only items whose due date is at or before now are listed, and an item with no due date never appears under any option except **No due date**.
- [ ] AC3: Given the server UI timezone, when **Due today** is selected, then only items due on today's calendar date are listed. When **Due this week** is selected, only items due between Monday 00:00 and Sunday 23:59:59 of the current week are listed. When **Due soon** is selected, only items due after now and within the same window as the "Due soon" badge (`NearDueDuration`, 72h) are listed, so every open row shows the "Due soon" badge.
- [ ] AC4: When **Has a due date** is selected, only items with a due date are listed. When **No due date** is selected, only items without one are listed. Together the two options cover the unfiltered list exactly.
- [ ] AC5: Given a selected due-date option, then the Open/Closed counts and the pagination reflect the filter, and the state tabs, search box, other filter dropdowns and page links keep `due=` in their URLs. The filter combines with state, labels, milestone, project, assignee, poster and keyword search.
- [ ] AC6: Given an issue whose due date was just changed, when the dashboard is searched with a keyword and a due-date option, then the result uses the new due date.
- [ ] AC7: Given an unknown value such as `?due=bogus`, when the page loads, then the list is unfiltered and no error is shown.

## Out of Scope
- The single-milestone issue page, the `/issues/search` JSON endpoints and the REST API (`/api/v1/.../issues`).
- Custom date ranges ("due between X and Y") and a configurable first day of the week.
- Filtering by the milestone's due date; only the issue's own due date is used.
- Changing how the overdue / due-soon badge itself is calculated.
- Translations other than en-US (handled by the project's translation process).

## Open Questions
- None.

## Design Decision

### Decision 1
**Decision:** Translate `?due=` once, in a shared route-level parser, into plain deadline bounds (`DeadlineAfterUnix`, `DeadlineBeforeUnix`, `HasDeadline`) on `IssuesOptions` and the issue indexer's `SearchOptions`, next to the existing `UpdatedAfterUnix` / `UpdatedBeforeUnix` pair.
**Alternatives Considered:** (a) A named filter (`overdue`, `soon`, ...) passed down to the model, whose SQL reproduces the badge's open/closed rules (a closed issue is overdue only if it was closed after its deadline). (b) Filtering rows in the browser after the page loads.
**Rationale:** Plain ranges work the same in the database and in every search backend (bleve, Elasticsearch, Meilisearch), which the dashboard relies on for keyword searches. Option (a) needs a `closed_unix` against `deadline_unix` comparison that the search backends cannot express. Option (b) breaks counts and pagination. One parser means one clock: "now" comes from `timeutil.TimeStampNow()`, the same clock the badge uses. "Due soon" reuses `NearDueDuration`, so on the Open tab the filter and the badge always agree.
**Consequences:** On the Closed and All tabs, a closed issue matches **Overdue** by its deadline alone, even if it was closed on time and so shows no Overdue badge. Every bound also forces `deadline_unix != 0`, so items with no due date (stored as 0) can never leak into Overdue. Meilisearch needs `deadline_unix` made filterable, which bumps its index version (a one-time re-index on upgrade). Changing an issue's due date now re-indexes it, otherwise a keyword search would filter on the old date.

### Decision 2
**Decision:** "Due this week" is the calendar week, Monday 00:00 to Sunday 23:59:59, in the server UI timezone (`[time] DEFAULT_UI_LOCATION`), the same timezone due dates are saved in.
**Alternatives Considered:** A rolling 7 days (today through today+6); a Sunday-to-Saturday week.
**Rationale:** It matches the label literally, follows ISO 8601 (Gitea has no week-start setting), and stays clearly different from "Due soon", which is already a rolling 72 hours.
**Consequences:** Late in the week the option looks only a few days ahead, and it includes items that went overdue earlier in the same week. Sunday-first users see a Monday-first week.

## Scope
medium (`scope: medium`). One set of query options, one parser and one dropdown shared by four pages. No schema change, since `deadline_unix` already exists and is indexed. The search-backend support and re-index on due-date change add some work.

```

```text
// Copy returns a copy of the options.
// Be careful, it's not a deep copy, so `SearchOptions.RepoIDs = {...}` is OK while `SearchOptions.RepoIDs[0] = ...` is not.
func (o *SearchOptions) Copy(edit ...func(options *SearchOptions)) *SearchOptions {
	if o == nil {
		return nil
	}
	v := *o
	for _, e := range edit {
		e(&v)
	}
	return &v
}

// used for optimized issue index based search
func (o *SearchOptions) IsKeywordNumeric() bool {
	_, err := strconv.Atoi(o.Keyword)
	return err == nil
}

type SortBy string

const (
	SortByCreatedDesc  SortBy = "-created_unix"
	SortByUpdatedDesc  SortBy = "-updated_unix"
	SortByCommentsDesc SortBy = "-comment_count"
	SortByDeadlineDesc SortBy = "-deadline_unix"
```

```go
// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package issue

import (
	"time"

	issues_model "gitea.dev/models/issues"
	"gitea.dev/modules/optional"
)

// DueDateFilter is the "due" query parameter of the issue lists, resolved to inclusive deadline bounds
type DueDateFilter struct {
	Name        string // the query value, empty when absent or unknown
	AfterUnix   int64
	BeforeUnix  int64
	HasDeadline optional.Option[bool]
}

// ParseDueDateFilter resolves the "due" query parameter against now. Calendar options use now's
// location, so callers pass a time in setting.DefaultUILocation, where deadlines are pinned to the
// end of their day. An unknown value silently turns the filter off, so a stale link still renders.
func ParseDueDateFilter(due string, now time.Time) DueDateFilter {
	f := DueDateFilter{Name: due, HasDeadline: optional.Some(true)}
	y, m, d := now.Date()
	switch due {
	case "overdue":
		// same comparisons as the overdue and near-due badges
		f.BeforeUnix = now.Unix()
	case "soon":
		f.AfterUnix = now.Unix() + 1
		f.BeforeUnix = now.Add(issues_model.NearDueDuration).Unix()
	case "today":
		f.AfterUnix = time.Date(y, m, d, 0, 0, 0, 0, now.Location()).Unix()
		f.BeforeUnix = time.Date(y, m, d+1, 0, 0, 0, 0, now.Location()).Unix() - 1
	case "week":
		monday := d - (int(now.Weekday())+6)%7 // weeks start on Monday, as in ISO 8601
		f.AfterUnix = time.Date(y, m, monday, 0, 0, 0, 0, now.Location()).Unix()
		f.BeforeUnix = time.Date(y, m, monday+7, 0, 0, 0, 0, now.Location()).Unix() - 1
	case "set":
	case "none":
		f.HasDeadline = optional.Some(false)
	default:
		return DueDateFilter{}
	}
	return f
}

// Apply narrows opts to the issues the filter matches
func (f DueDateFilter) Apply(opts *issues_model.IssuesOptions) {
	opts.DeadlineAfterUnix = f.AfterUnix
	opts.DeadlineBeforeUnix = f.BeforeUnix
	opts.HasDeadline = f.HasDeadline
}
```

```go
// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package issue

import (
	"testing"
	"time"

	issues_model "gitea.dev/models/issues"
	"gitea.dev/modules/optional"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

func TestParseDueDateFilter(t *testing.T) {
	loc, err := time.LoadLocation("America/New_York")
	require.NoError(t, err)
	wednesday := time.Date(2026, 10, 7, 15, 30, 0, 0, loc)
	local := func(unix int64) string { // "" for an unset bound
		if unix == 0 {
			return ""
		}
		return time.Unix(unix, 0).In(loc).Format(time.DateTime)
	}

	cases := []struct {
		name          string
		due           string
		now           time.Time
		after, before string
		hasDeadline   optional.Option[bool]
	}{
		{"overdue is anything due up to now", "overdue", wednesday, "", "2026-10-07 15:30:00", optional.Some(true)},
		{"soon is the near-due badge window", "soon", wednesday, "2026-10-07 15:30:01", local(wednesday.Add(issues_model.NearDueDuration).Unix()), optional.Some(true)},
		{"today is the local calendar day", "today", wednesday, "2026-10-07 00:00:00", "2026-10-07 23:59:59", optional.Some(true)},
		{"today on the 25-hour day daylight saving ends", "today", time.Date(2026, 11, 1, 12, 0, 0, 0, loc), "2026-11-01 00:00:00", "2026-11-01 23:59:59", optional.Some(true)},
		{"week runs Monday to Sunday", "week", wednesday, "2026-10-05 00:00:00", "2026-10-11 23:59:59", optional.Some(true)},
		{"week on its first second", "week", time.Date(2026, 10, 5, 0, 0, 0, 0, loc), "2026-10-05 00:00:00", "2026-10-11 23:59:59", optional.Some(true)},
		{"week on its last second", "week", time.Date(2026, 10, 11, 23, 59, 59, 0, loc), "2026-10-05 00:00:00", "2026-10-11 23:59:59", optional.Some(true)},
		{"week across the end of daylight saving", "week", time.Date(2026, 10, 28, 9, 0, 0, 0, loc), "2026-10-26 00:00:00", "2026-11-01 23:59:59", optional.Some(true)},
		{"set has no bounds", "set", wednesday, "", "", optional.Some(true)},
		{"none matches undated issues", "none", wednesday, "", "", optional.Some(false)},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			f := ParseDueDateFilter(c.due, c.now)
			assert.Equal(t, c.due, f.Name)
			assert.Equal(t, c.after, local(f.AfterUnix))
			assert.Equal(t, c.before, local(f.BeforeUnix))
			assert.Equal(t, c.hasDeadline, f.HasDeadline)
		})
	}

	t.Run("unknown values turn the filter off", func(t *testing.T) {
		for _, due := range []string{"", "bogus", "Overdue"} {
			assert.Equal(t, DueDateFilter{}, ParseDueDateFilter(due, wednesday), due)
		}
	})

	t.Run("apply copies the bounds", func(t *testing.T) {
		opts := &issues_model.IssuesOptions{}
		ParseDueDateFilter("today", wednesday).Apply(opts)
		assert.Equal(t, "2026-10-07 00:00:00", local(opts.DeadlineAfterUnix))
		assert.Equal(t, "2026-10-07 23:59:59", local(opts.DeadlineBeforeUnix))
		assert.Equal(t, optional.Some(true), opts.HasDeadline)
	})
}

```

```text
func TestIndexer(t *testing.T, indexer internal.Indexer) {
	_, err := indexer.Init(t.Context())
	require.NoError(t, err)

	require.NoError(t, indexer.Ping(t.Context()))

	var (
		ids  []int64
		data = map[int64]*internal.IndexerData{}
	)
	{
		d := generateDefaultIndexerData()
		for _, v := range d {
			ids = append(ids, v.ID)
			data[v.ID] = v
		}
		require.NoError(t, indexer.Index(t.Context(), d...))
		waitData(t, indexer, int64(len(data)))
	}

	defer func() {
		require.NoError(t, indexer.Delete(t.Context(), ids...))
	}()

	for _, c := range cases {
		t.Run(c.Name, func(t *testing.T) {
			if len(c.ExtraData) > 0 {
				require.NoError(t, indexer.Index(t.Context(), c.ExtraData...))
				for _, v := range c.ExtraData {
					data[v.ID] = v
				}
				waitData(t, indexer, int64(len(data)))
				defer func() {
					for _, v := range c.ExtraData {
						require.NoError(t, indexer.Delete(t.Context(), v.ID))
						delete(data, v.ID)
					}
					waitData(t, indexer, int64(len(data)))
				}()
			}

			result, err := indexer.Search(t.Context(), c.SearchOptions)
			require.NoError(t, err)

			if c.Expected != nil {
				c.Expected(t, data, result)
			} else {
				ids := make([]int64, 0, len(result.Hits))
				for _, hit := range result.Hits {
					ids = append(ids, hit.ID)
				}
				assert.Equal(t, c.ExpectedIDs, ids)
				assert.Equal(t, c.ExpectedTotal, result.Total)
			}

			// test counting
			c.SearchOptions.Paginator = &db.ListOptions{PageSize: 0}
			countResult, err := indexer.Search(t.Context(), c.SearchOptions)
			require.NoError(t, err)
			assert.Empty(t, countResult.Hits)
			assert.Equal(t, result.Total, countResult.Total)
		})
	}
```
```text
}

func countIndexerData(data map[int64]*internal.IndexerData, f func(v *internal.IndexerData) bool) int64 {
	var count int64
	for _, v := range data {
		if f(v) {
			count++
		}
	}
	return count
}

// waitData waits for the indexer to index all data.
// Some engines like Elasticsearch index data asynchronously, so we need to wait for a while.
func waitData(t *testing.T, indexer internal.Indexer, total int64) {
	assert.Eventually(t, func() bool {
		result, err := indexer.Search(t.Context(), &internal.SearchOptions{Paginator: &db.ListOptions{}})
		require.NoError(t, err)
		return result.Total == total
	}, 10*time.Second, 100*time.Millisecond, "expected total=%d", total)
}
```

```text
// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package integration

import (
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	issues_model "gitea.dev/models/issues"
	"gitea.dev/models/unittest"
	"gitea.dev/tests"

	"github.com/PuerkitoBio/goquery"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

// newExclusiveLabel creates an exclusive scoped label on user2/repo1 and returns its id.
func newExclusiveLabel(t *testing.T, sess *TestSession, name string, order int) int64 {
	t.Helper()
	req := NewRequestWithValues(t, "POST", "/user2/repo1/labels/new", map[string]string{
		"title":           name,
		"color":           "#112233",
		"exclusive":       "on",
		"exclusive_order": strconv.Itoa(order),
	})
	sess.MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusOK) // NewLabel answers with ctx.JSONRedirect
	label := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Label{RepoID: 1, Name: name})
	require.True(t, label.Exclusive, "%s must be exclusive, or its scope does not exist", name)
	return label.ID
}

func attachIssueLabel(t *testing.T, sess *TestSession, issueID, labelID int64) {
	t.Helper()
	req := NewRequestWithValues(t, "POST", fmt.Sprintf("/user2/repo1/issues/labels?issue_ids=%d", issueID), map[string]string{
		"action": "attach",
		"id":     strconv.FormatInt(labelID, 10),
	})
	sess.MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusOK)
}

// pullListGroups returns, per rendered group, its summary text and the issue indexes inside it.
func pullListGroups(t *testing.T, sess *TestSession, query string) (summaries []string, indexes [][]string) {
	t.Helper()
	req := NewRequest(t, "GET", "/user2/repo1/pulls?"+query)
	resp := sess.MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusOK)
	NewHTMLParser(t, resp.Body).doc.Find("details.issue-list-group").Each(func(_ int, group *goquery.Selection) {
		summaries = append(summaries, strings.Join(strings.Fields(group.Find("summary").Text()), " "))
		var groupIndexes []string
		group.Find(".item-body .index").Each(func(_ int, index *goquery.Selection) {
			groupIndexes = append(groupIndexes, strings.TrimSpace(index.Text()))
		})
		indexes = append(indexes, groupIndexes)
	})
	return summaries, indexes
}
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

func getIssuesSelection(t testing.TB, htmlDoc *HTMLDoc) *goquery.Selection {
	issueList := htmlDoc.doc.Find("#issue-list")
	assert.Equal(t, 1, issueList.Length())
	return issueList.Find(".item").Find(".list-item-large-title")
}

func getIssue(t *testing.T, repoID int64, issueSelection *goquery.Selection) *issues_model.Issue {
	href, exists := issueSelection.Attr("href")
	assert.True(t, exists)
	indexStr := href[strings.LastIndexByte(href, '/')+1:]
	index, err := strconv.Atoi(indexStr)
	assert.NoError(t, err, "Invalid issue href: %s", href)
	return unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{RepoID: repoID, Index: int64(index)})
```

```go
package integration

import (

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

func TestIssueDueDateFilter(t *testing.T) {
	defer tests.PrepareTestEnv(t)()
	defer timeutil.MockSet(time.Date(2026, 10, 7, 12, 0, 0, 0, setting.DefaultUILocation))() // a Wednesday

	session := loginUser(t, "user2")
	setDeadline := func(index int64, date string) {
		req := NewRequestWithValues(t, "POST", fmt.Sprintf("/user2/repo1/issues/%d/deadline", index), map[string]string{"deadline": date})
		session.MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusOK)
	}
	// user2/repo1 holds issue #1, closed issue #4 and pulls #2, #3 and #5, none with a deadline in the fixtures
	deadlines := map[int64]string{1: "2026-10-06", 2: "2026-10-07", 4: "2026-10-08", 5: "2026-10-30"}
	for index, date := range deadlines {
		setDeadline(index, date)
	}
	defer func() { // the issue indexer outlives the test database, so leave it as the fixtures had it
		for index := range deadlines {
			setDeadline(index, "")
		}
	}()

	list := func(t *testing.T, url string) (doc *HTMLDoc, links []string) {
		t.Helper()
		resp := session.MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", url), http.StatusOK)
		doc = NewHTMLParser(t, resp.Body)
		doc.Find("#issue-list .list-item-large-title").Each(func(_ int, a *goquery.Selection) {
			links = append(links, a.AttrOr("href", ""))
		})
		return doc, links
	}

	t.Run("repo issues", func(t *testing.T) {
		_, links := list(t, "/user2/repo1/issues?state=all&due=overdue")
		assert.Equal(t, []string{"/user2/repo1/issues/1"}, links)

		_, links = list(t, "/user2/repo1/issues?state=all&due=soon")
		assert.Equal(t, []string{"/user2/repo1/issues/4"}, links, "a closed issue matches by its deadline alone")
	})

	t.Run("repo pulls", func(t *testing.T) {
		for due, expected := range map[string][]string{
			"today": {"/user2/repo1/pulls/2"},
			"week":  {"/user2/repo1/pulls/2"},
			"set":   {"/user2/repo1/pulls/2", "/user2/repo1/pulls/5"},
			"none":  {"/user2/repo1/pulls/3"},
			"bogus": {"/user2/repo1/pulls/2", "/user2/repo1/pulls/3", "/user2/repo1/pulls/5"},
		} {
			_, links := list(t, "/user2/repo1/pulls?due="+due)
			assert.ElementsMatch(t, expected, links, due)
		}

		doc, _ := list(t, "/user2/repo1/pulls?due=set")
		assert.Equal(t, "2 Open", strings.Join(strings.Fields(doc.Find(".small-menu-items .item").First().Text()), " "))
		assert.Equal(t, "Has a due date", strings.TrimSpace(doc.Find(".due-date-filter .active.item").Text()))
		doc.Find(".small-menu-items a").Each(func(_ int, a *goquery.Selection) {
			assert.Contains(t, a.AttrOr("href", ""), "due=set")
		})
		assert.Contains(t, doc.Find(`a[href*="sort=oldest"]`).AttrOr("href", ""), "due=set")
		assert.Equal(t, "set", doc.Find(`.issue-list-search input[name="due"]`).AttrOr("value", ""))
	})

	t.Run("dashboard", func(t *testing.T) {
		doc, links := list(t, "/pulls?due=today")
		assert.Equal(t, []string{"/user2/repo1/pulls/2"}, links)
		assert.Equal(t, 1, doc.Find(".due-date-filter").Length())

		_, links = list(t, "/pulls?due=none")
		assert.Contains(t, links, "/user2/repo1/pulls/3")
		assert.NotContains(t, links, "/user2/repo1/pulls/2")

		// a keyword search filters in the issue indexer, which has to have picked up the new deadline
		require.Eventually(t, func() bool {
			_, links := list(t, "/pulls?q=issue2&due=today")
			return slices.Equal([]string{"/user2/repo1/pulls/2"}, links)
		}, 5*time.Second, 50*time.Millisecond)

		doc, _ = list(t, "/org/org3/issues")
		assert.Equal(t, 1, doc.Find(".due-date-filter").Length())
	})

	t.Run("milestone page ignores the filter", func(t *testing.T) {
		doc, links := list(t, "/user2/repo1/milestone/1?due=none")
		assert.Equal(t, 0, doc.Find(".due-date-filter").Length())
		assert.Equal(t, []string{"/user2/repo1/pulls/2"}, links) // has a deadline, so a filter would have hidden it
	})
}
```

```python
import base64, http.cookiejar, json, re, sys, urllib.parse, urllib.request
from html.parser import HTMLParser

BASE = "http://localhost:3333"
USER, PW = "verifier", "Verify-due-34!"
REPO = "/jackd/testtest"

jar = http.cookiejar.CookieJar()
opener = urllib.request.build_opener(urllib.request.HTTPCookieProcessor(jar))

def get(path):
    with opener.open(BASE + path) as r:
        return r.status, r.read().decode()

def csrf(html):
    return re.search(r'name="_csrf" value="([^"]+)"', html).group(1)

def post(path, fields, token):
    data = urllib.parse.urlencode({**fields, "_csrf": token}).encode()
    with opener.open(urllib.request.Request(BASE + path, data=data, headers={"X-Csrf-Token": token})) as r:
        return r.status

def api(method, path, body=None):
    req = urllib.request.Request(BASE + "/api/v1" + path, method=method, data=json.dumps(body).encode() if body else None,
                                 headers={"Content-Type": "application/json",
                                          "Authorization": "Basic " + base64.b64encode(f"{USER}:{PW}".encode()).decode()})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as r:
        return r.status

class Page(HTMLParser):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__(); self.rows, self.due_items, self.in_due, self.depth, self.open_tab, self.cap = [], [], False, 0, None, None
    def handle_starttag(self, tag, attrs):
        a = dict(attrs); cls = a.get("class") or ""
        if tag == "div" and "due-date-filter" in cls: self.in_due, self.depth = True, 0
        if self.in_due and tag == "div": self.depth += 1
        if tag == "a" and "list-item-large-title" in cls: self.rows.append(a["href"])
        if self.in_due and tag == "a": self.cap = ["active" in cls, a["href"], ""]
    def handle_endtag(self, tag):
        if self.in_due and tag == "a" and self.cap: self.due_items.append(tuple(self.cap)); self.cap = None
        if self.in_due and tag == "div":
            self.depth -= 1
            if self.depth == 0: self.in_due = False
    def handle_data(self, data):
        if self.cap is not None: self.cap[2] += data.strip()

def page(path):
    status, html = get(path)
    p = Page(); p.feed(html)
    tabs = re.findall(r'(\d+)(?:&nbsp;|\s)+(Open|Closed)', html)
    return status, p, tabs

if sys.argv[1] == "setup":
    _, html = get("/user/login")
    post("/user/login", {"user_name": USER, "password": PW}, csrf(html))
    _, html = get(REPO + "/issues/1")

    print("deadline #1 ->", post(REPO + "/issues/1/deadline", {"deadline": sys.argv[2]}, token))
    print("deadline #2 ->", post(REPO + "/issues/2/deadline", {"deadline": sys.argv[3]}, token))
    print("new issue  ->", api("POST", "/repos/jackd/testtest/issues", {"title": "No due date here"}))
else:
    _, html = get("/user/login")
    post("/user/login", {"user_name": USER, "password": PW}, csrf(html))
    for path in sys.argv[2:]:
        status, p, tabs = page(path)
        active = [t for a, _, t in p.due_items if a]
        print(f"{path}\n  {status} rows={p.rows} tabs={tabs[:2]} dropdown={'yes' if p.due_items else 'no'} active={active}")
        if sys.argv[1] == "links" and p.due_items:
            for a, href, text in p.due_items: print(f"    {'*' if a else ' '} {text:16} {href}")
```

```text
## The guide layer (rules 16-22)

`guide/` holds a plain-English page for each reference page in `docs/`, same filename. It exists so
a person new to Go and to this codebase can get oriented. It is **derived**, not independent.

16. Every guide carries `source:`, `source-hash:` and `verified-at:` in its frontmatter **[checked]**.
17. A guide's `source:` names a real `docs/*.md` with the **same filename** **[checked]**.
18. `source-hash:` is the first 16 characters of `sha256sum docs/<name>.md`. If the reference page
    changes and the guide is not regenerated, `check.sh` reports **drift** **[checked]**. Regenerating
    means: reread the reference page, rewrite the guide, update the hash and `verified-at`.
19. Guide headings match `guide/_TEMPLATE.md` exactly and in order **[checked]**.
20. Guides are capped at **200 lines**, code fences at **30** **[checked]** — teaching needs more room
    than reference does.
21. **A guide adds explanation, vocabulary and worked steps. It adds no new facts.** Every repo path
    a guide cites must also be cited by its source page **[checked]**. If you need a fact the
    reference page lacks, add it *there* first, which bumps the hash and forces the guide to be
    regenerated in the same commit — exactly the intended order.
22. `guide/START-HERE.md` has no source page. It is exempt from rules 17, 18 and 21, and is where
    cross-cutting material lives that no single reference page owns.

**Never fix a fact in `guide/`.** If the two layers disagree, the reference page is the truth and
the guide is stale: fix `docs/`, regenerate the guide, ship both in one PR. A disagreement is a bug
report against `docs/`, not an editing job in `guide/`.

**Known limitation:** a hand-edit to a guide that only rewords prose is not mechanically
detectable. Rule 21 catches invented facts; rule 18 catches a stale guide; review catches the rest.

## Updating `verified-at`

`verified-at` is the short SHA the doc was last checked against, from `git rev-parse --short HEAD`.
Bump it whenever you confirm or correct a doc. A doc whose `verified-at` is far behind `main` has
not been checked recently — treat its details as hints and confirm them in the code before relying
on them.
```

```text
# modules/* infrastructure — queues, cache, storage, indexers, locks

**Read when:** work needs to happen asynchronously, be cached, be stored as a file, be searchable,
or be serialised across processes.
**Not here:** configuration -> `modules-setting.md`; the database -> `models-db.md`.

## Responsibilities

| Package | Owns |
| --- | --- |
| `modules/queue` | persistent worker-pool queues (channel, leveldb, redis backends) |
| `modules/cache` | the key/value cache, including a request-scoped layer |
| `modules/storage` | blob storage for attachments, LFS, avatars, artifacts (local, minio, azure) |
| `modules/indexer` | code, issue and stats indexers (bleve, elasticsearch, meilisearch, db) |
| `modules/globallock` | cross-process locks (memory or redis) |
| `modules/log` | logging |
| `modules/graceful` | graceful startup, shutdown and restart |
| `modules/process` | the process manager behind long-running commands |

## Key files

| Path | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `modules/queue/manager.go` | `CreateSimpleQueue`, `CreateUniqueQueue` |
| `modules/queue/workergroup.go` | the worker pool behind `WorkerPoolQueue[T]` |
| `modules/queue/base_channel.go`, `base_levelqueue.go`, `base_redis.go` | the backends |
| `modules/cache/cache.go`, `string_cache.go`, `context.go` | the cache API and the request-scoped cache |
| `modules/globallock/globallock.go`, `locker.go` | `Lock` and the locker implementations |
| `modules/indexer/issues/`, `code/`, `stats/` | one subtree per index |
| `modules/storage/storage.go` | the storage interface and its backends |

## Conventions & invariants

- **Queues are how Gitea does background work.** `CreateSimpleQueue` and `CreateUniqueQueue` return
  a `WorkerPoolQueue[T]`; a *unique* queue deduplicates by item, which is why pushing the same PR
  id twice is free (`services-pull-and-gitdiff.md`) and why the Actions job emitter can enqueue
  freely (`services-actions.md`).
- A queue is created once at startup and its handler must be idempotent: items can be retried after
  a restart, and a persistent backend replays what was not acknowledged.
- **Queue payloads must survive serialisation** — push an id, not a loaded struct with unexported
  fields or pointers to models.
- `globallock.Lock` is for mutual exclusion *across processes*, not a `sync.Mutex`. It is what
  makes things like the versioned migration safe when several instances start at once.
- Cached values must tolerate being absent. The request-scoped cache in `modules/cache/context.go`
  lives for one request and is the right place for "load this once per request".
- Indexers are eventually consistent. A freshly created issue is in the database immediately and in
  the index shortly after, so a list built from the index can lag — never use an index as the
  source of truth for correctness.
- `modules/storage` returns an interface; never assume a local filesystem path, because minio and
  azure backends are supported.

## Recipes

**Do work in the background.** Create a unique queue at startup with a handler that takes ids, and
push from wherever the triggering change happens. Copy `services/actions/job_emitter.go` or
`services/pull/check.go`.

**Cache an expensive per-request value.** Use the request-scoped cache rather than a package-level
map, so it cannot leak between users.

**Serialise something across instances.** `globallock.Lock(ctx, "<name>")`, and always release
through the returned function.

## Gotchas

- A queue handler that panics loses the item; handle errors and return rather than panicking.
- A non-unique queue plus a frequent trigger produces unbounded duplicate work — pick
  `CreateUniqueQueue` unless duplicates are meaningful.
- Redis-backed queues, caches and locks are only active when configured; behaviour differs between
  a local SQLite dev instance and production, so test the non-redis path too.
- Search results come from the indexer, so "the issue exists but does not appear in search" is
  usually an indexing lag or a missing reindex, not a query bug.

## Related

- `modules-setting.md` — how each of these is configured
- `services-actions.md`, `services-pull-and-gitdiff.md` — the two heaviest queue users
```

```text
7	<!-- Derived from docs/models-issues.md. Do not edit by hand: fix the reference doc and regenerate

9
10	# Issues and pull requests in the database, in plain English
11
12	**In one sentence:** one table holds both issues and pull requests, most of what you think of as
13	"the issue" is loaded separately on demand, and the number in the URL is not the primary key.
14	**Come here when:** you are querying or changing issues, pull requests, comments, labels, milestones
15	or reviews.
16
17	## What this is
18
19	The database side of the whole issue domain — and in Gitea, **pull requests live here too**, because
20	a pull request is an issue with extra columns.
21
22	The files divide by concern: issue core, pull requests, comments, reviews, labels and milestones,
23	people and time tracking, and the relationships between issues.
24
25	There is also a separate small package, `models/pull`, which despite its name is not where pull
26	requests live. It holds only automerge scheduling and per-user review state.
27
28	## Why it exists
29
30	**Why one table for two things?** Because an issue and a pull request are the same thing to almost
31	all of Gitea. Both have a title, a description, comments, labels, a milestone, assignees, an
32	open/closed state and a number. If they were separate tables, every one of those features would need
33	implementing twice. Instead there is one `issue` row with a flag, and the handful of pull-request-only
34	columns live in a second row linked to it.
35
36	**Why is so much loaded separately?** An issue row does not contain its author, labels, milestone or
37	comments — those are other tables. Fetching all of them every time would make listing a hundred
38	issues enormously expensive when the list page needs only a few. So the row comes back with those
39	fields empty and you load what you actually need.
40
41	That is a good trade, and it produces the single most common bug in this area: **reading a field
42	nobody loaded and getting an empty value rather than an error.**
43
44	## Words you'll meet
45
46	- **discriminator** — a column saying which kind of thing a row is. Here, `IsPull`.
47	- **primary key** — the globally unique `ID`.
48	- **per-repository index** — the number users see (`#42`), which restarts at 1 in every repository.
49	- **loader** — a `LoadXxx(ctx)` method that fills in one of those empty fields.
50	- **idempotent** — calling it twice does the same as calling it once.
51	- **denormalised counter** — a count stored on another row for speed, which then has to be kept
52	  correct by hand.
53	- **N+1** — fetching *n* things and then running *n* more queries, one per item.
54	- **sentinel error** — a shared error value that code elsewhere can test for.
55	- **JSON field** — one column holding a small bundle of named values, saved as JSON text.
56
57	## What's in these files
58
59	| Where | What it is for |
60	| --- | --- |
61	| `models/issues/issue.go` | The `Issue` struct itself, its loaders, and its "not found" error. |
62	| `models/issues/issue_list.go` | `IssueList` — a slice of issues that can load everything for all of them at once. |
63	| `models/issues/pull.go` | The pull-request-only row. |
64	| `models/issues/comment.go` | Comments, and the enum of comment kinds. |
65	| `models/issues/issue_close_reason.go` | Why an issue or pull request was closed: the `CloseReason` values and their names, which ones each kind may use, which ones the list's bulk Close offers, which one the close button starts on, and the check that refuses a bad one. Saved in three columns on `Issue`. |
66	| `models/issues/issue_label.go` | Labels on issues — and the clearest small example of the loader pattern. |
67	| `models/issues/issue_index.go` | Recalculating per-repository numbering. |
68	| `models/issues/issue_group.go` | Splitting a list of issues into category groups, for the grouped ("folder") list view. |
69
70	The rest divide by area: `review.go` and `review_list.go`, `label.go`, `milestone.go`,
71	`assignees.go`, `stopwatch.go` and `tracked_time.go`, and the relationship files `dependency.go`,
72	`issue_xref.go`, `issue_watch.go`, `issue_pin.go`, `issue_lock.go`, `reaction.go`.
73
74	## The rules, and why
75
76	**`IsPull` decides what a row is.** A query that forgets it returns both issues and pull requests.
77	On an issues page that means pull requests appearing in the list; on a count, a number that is
78	always too high.
79
80	**`Index` is not `ID`.** `ID` is the global primary key. `Index` is the number in the URL, unique
81	only *within* a repository — so every repository has an issue `#1`. Looking something up from a URL
82	means matching on the repository **and** the index. Using the URL number as an `ID` finds a
83	completely unrelated issue in another repository, which is worse than an error because it looks like
84	it worked.
85
86	**Never set `Index` yourself.** It comes from the shared numbering helper, called inside the same
87	transaction that inserts the row. Assigning it by hand races with anyone else creating an issue in
88	that repository at the same moment.
89
90	**Fields tagged `xorm:"-"` are empty until you load them.** `Repo`, `Poster`, `Labels`,
91	`Milestone`, `Assignee`, `Attachments`, `Comments`, `PullRequest` and others are all filled in by a
92	matching `LoadXxx(ctx)` method. `LoadAttributes(ctx)` loads the usual set in one go.
93
94	**Loaders never refresh.** Each is guarded by an internal "already loaded" flag, so calling one
95	twice is free — but it also means a value that changed in the database after the first call **stays
96	stale on that struct**. If you need current data, re-fetch the issue; calling the loader again does
97	nothing.
98
99	**Errors come in three parts.** There is an `ErrIssueNotExist` struct, an `IsErrIssueNotExist(err)`
100	test, and an `Unwrap()` that returns a shared sentinel like `util.ErrNotExist`. That third part is
101	what lets a handler ask "is this a not-found error?" without importing every model package — and it
102	is what turns a missing issue into a 404 instead of a 500.
103
104	**Comment kinds are an enum**, and rendering branches on it. A plain comment and a review are both
105	comments with different kinds, as are all the "closed this", "added a label" timeline entries.
106	Adding a kind means handling it in the templates too, or it renders as nothing.
107
108	**Extra data on a comment goes in its metadata, not a new column.** `Comment` has a JSON field,
109	`CommentMetaData`, and its code comment in `comment.go` asks for any new non-index data to go there.
110	It is written once, when the comment is created, and never changed — which suits a timeline, where
111	each entry records what was true at that moment. The cost is that SQL cannot search, sort or index
112	on anything inside it.
113
114	**A close reason travels as a word, not a number.** The database stores each reason as a number,
115	but forms and pages send its name instead: `not_planned`, not `2`. `CloseReason.String` turns a
116	reason into its name and `AsCloseReason` turns a name back, the same way `CommentType.String` and
117	`AsCommentType` work for comment kinds. Because pages send these names, a name can no more be
118	changed than its number can.
119
120	**A close comment keeps its own copy of the reason.** The issue's reason describes the *current*
121	close; the comment's copy, in `CommentMetaData`, describes *that* close and never changes. Read it
122	with `Comment.MetaCloseReason()` rather than reaching into the metadata yourself: close comments
123	written before this feature existed have no metadata at all, and the method turns that into "no
124	reason" instead of an error.
125
126	**A duplicate is typed as a number but stored as an ID.** Closing as a duplicate of `#12` looks
127	`#12` up in the issue's own repository (`GetIssueByIndex`, inside `SetIssueAsClosed`), so a number
128	from another repository is refused. What gets stored is that issue's global ID. `Comment.LoadCloseDuplicateIssue` turns the ID back into the
129	issue, repository included; if the target has since been deleted, it reports "not found" instead
130	of breaking the page.
131
132	**Reopening wipes the issue's reason, not the comment's.** `setIssueAsReopen` is the only code that
133	reopens anything, and it clears the reason, text and duplicate target on the issue. The close
134	comment keeps what was true when it was written.
135
136	## How to actually do it
137
138	**Display a list of issues.** Fetch into an `IssueList`, then call `LoadAttributes(ctx)` **once, on
139	the list**. That type exists precisely to load everything for every issue in a handful of queries.
140	Looping and calling the single-issue loader is the N+1 it was built to prevent, and it is the
141	difference between a fast page and a slow one.
142
143	**Add a column to `Issue`.** Add the field with its tag, write a migration, and if the value
144	duplicates something stored elsewhere, extend the consistency check in `models/main_test.go` and the
145	fixtures.
146
147	**Get the pull request for an issue.** `issue.LoadPullRequest(ctx)`, then read `issue.PullRequest`.
148	Going the other way, use the pull request's own loader and then `pr.Issue`.
149
150	## Traps, and what they look like
151
152	**A field is empty and you are sure it has data.** You did not call its loader. There is no error
153	for this — the field is simply the zero value. Check for the `LoadXxx` call before you check the
154	database.
155
156	**You changed something and the struct still shows the old value.** Loaders do not refresh. Re-fetch
157	the issue.
158
159	**Pull requests show up on the issues page, or a count is too high.** A query missing the `IsPull`
160	condition.
161
162	**You looked up issue `#42` and got somebody else's issue.** You used the URL number as an `ID`.
163	Match repository plus index.
164
165	**A test you did not touch fails on a consistency check.** The repository row stores counts —
166	`NumIssues`, `NumClosedIssues`, `NumPulls` and friends — alongside the real issues. Changing issue
167	state, or adding a fixture row, means keeping those in step.
168
169	**You grouped the list by category and a group appears twice, or in a different place, on page 2.**
170	The grouping is worked out in two places that must agree: `applyGroupByLabelScope` in
171	`models/issues/issue_search.go` sorts the rows in SQL so that one page's issues of the same category
172	sit together, and `GroupByExclusiveLabelScope` in `models/issues/issue_group.go` then cuts that page
173	into groups in Go. If you change the order in one, change it in the other. In particular both settle
174	ties on the label's `id`, not its name, because the database and Go do not sort text the same way.
175
176	**`Test_MigrateFromGiteaToGitea` fails with "missing fixture" after you add a column to `Issue`.** The
177	migration code fetches issues in pages sized by `db.MaxBatchInsertSize` (`models/db/engine.go`): 999
178	divided by the number of columns. One more column changes the page size, the request asks for a
179	different `limit`, and the recorded response in
180	`tests/integration/_mock_data/Test_MigrateFromGiteaToGitea/` no longer matches its name. Rename that
181	file to the new `limit`; its contents stay valid while the repository has fewer issues than the page size.
182
183	**Building an issue's link crashes with a nil pointer.** `Issue.Link()` reads `issue.Repo`, and
184	`GetIssueByID` does not fill it in. Call `LoadRepo(ctx)` first.
185
186	**You go looking for pull requests in `models/pull` and it is nearly empty.** Pull requests are in
187	`models/issues/pull.go`. `models/pull` only holds automerge and review state. Both `Issue` and
188	`PullRequest` also carry an `Index`; they agree, and you should write through the issue.
189
190	## Where to go next
191
192	- `docs/models-issues.md` (in this folder) — the reference page this was written from
193	- `models-db.md` — transactions and the numbering helper
194	- `models-repo-and-git.md` — those counter columns, and the per-repo feature switches
```

```text
// Init initializes the indexer
func (i *Indexer) Init(_ context.Context) (bool, error) {
	if i == nil {
		return false, errors.New("cannot init nil indexer")
	}

	if i.Client != nil {
		return false, errors.New("indexer is already initialized")
	}

	i.Client = meilisearch.New(i.url, meilisearch.WithAPIKey(i.apiKey))
	_, err := i.Client.GetIndex(i.VersionedIndexName())
	if err == nil {
		return true, nil
	}
	_, err = i.Client.CreateIndex(&meilisearch.IndexConfig{
		Uid:        i.VersionedIndexName(),
		PrimaryKey: "id",
	})
	if err != nil {
		return false, err
	}

	i.checkOldIndexes()

	_, err = i.Client.Index(i.VersionedIndexName()).UpdateSettings(i.settings)
	return false, err
}
```

````markdown
Title: feat(issues): filter issues and pull requests by due date

Closes #34

## What changed

Adds a **Due date** dropdown to the repository Issues and Pull Requests lists and to the dashboard Issues and Pull Requests pages (including the organization view of the dashboard). It offers All due dates, Overdue, Due today, Due this week, Due soon, Has a due date and No due date, and the choice is kept in the URL as `?due=...`.

- **One parser** (`routers/web/shared/issue/issue_due_date.go`) turns `?due=` into inclusive deadline bounds. "Now" comes from `timeutil.TimeStampNow()`, the clock the overdue/due-soon badge uses, and calendar options use the server UI timezone. "Due soon" reuses `issues_model.NearDueDuration`, and "this week" is Monday to Sunday. Unknown values are ignored.
- **Model:** `IssuesOptions` gets `DeadlineAfterUnix`, `DeadlineBeforeUnix` and `HasDeadline`, next to `UpdatedAfterUnix`/`UpdatedBeforeUnix`. They are applied in `applyConditions` (the list) **and** `applyIssuesOptions` (the Open/Closed counts and tracked time), which is a separate builder. Any bound also requires `deadline_unix != 0`, and "No due date" matches 0 or NULL.
- **Search indexers:** the same three options are carried through `SearchOptions` to the db, bleve, Elasticsearch and Meilisearch backends, because the dashboard filters through the indexer.
  - `SearchOptions.DeadlineRange()` folds the options into one range, so every backend has the same "no deadline" guard.
  - Meilisearch gets `deadline_unix` as a filterable attribute, and its index version goes from 6 to 7.
- **Re-index on due date change:** the new `issue_service.ChangeDeadline` wraps `issues_model.UpdateIssueDeadline` and queues the issue for re-indexing. The web and API deadline endpoints use it.
- **Templates:**
  - the new partial `templates/repo/issue/filter_item_due_date.tmpl` is used by `filter_list.tmpl` and `user/dashboard/issues.tmpl`;
  - `due` is threaded through the query link, the Open/Closed tabs and the search form's hidden inputs. Pagination already copies it.
- **Not on the milestone page:** the single-milestone issue page shares the list handler but stays unfiltered and shows no dropdown, as the issue covers only the issue and pull request lists.
- **Context docs:** `.claude-students/docs/models-issues.md` and `modules-infra.md` (and their guides) record the separate stats builder, the NULL deadline and the Meilisearch version rule.

## Why

Sorting by due date still buries the few overdue items among everything with no deadline. Since #3 added the overdue/due-soon badges, the obvious next step is "show me only those". This PR satisfies:

| AC | How it is met |
| --- | --- |
| AC1 | The dropdown appears on the four pages and not on the milestone page. |
| AC2 | Overdue lists only items with a due date at or before now. Undated items appear only under No due date. |
| AC3 | Due today, Due this week (Monday to Sunday) and Due soon behave as specified; Due soon uses the badge's window. |
| AC4 | Has a due date and No due date split the list. |
| AC5 | The counts and pagination follow the filter, the links keep `due=`, and it combines with the other filters. |
| AC6 | A dashboard keyword search sees a due date changed moments before, thanks to the re-index. |
| AC7 | `?due=bogus` is ignored. |

## How it was tested

| Test | What it covers |
| --- | --- |
| `routers/web/shared/issue/issue_due_date_test.go` (unit, no DB) | Every option's bounds, checked as local wall-clock times in America/New_York so they are not computed the same way as the code. Also: the first and last second of a week; a week and a day that cross the end of daylight saving (a 25-hour day); "soon" ending exactly at `NearDueDuration`; and unknown values. |
| `models/issues/issue_test.go` `TestIssuesDeadlineFilter` | Each option shape against both `Issues()` and `GetIssueStats()`, because the two use different condition builders. It includes the explicit guard case: an upper bound alone never returns undated rows. Writing this test found that fixture rows hold NULL, not 0, which is why "No due date" checks both. |
| `modules/indexer/issues/internal/tests/tests.go` | Four shared backend cases. Bleve runs them locally; Elasticsearch and Meilisearch run them where CI provides those services. |
| `modules/indexer/issues/indexer_test.go` | A db-indexer subtest for the same cases. |
| `tests/integration/issue_due_date_filter_test.go` (1.6s) | Fixes "now" with `timeutil.MockSet` and sets deadlines through the real deadline endpoint. It checks the rows for each option on the repo Issues and PR lists, the Open count, the active item, and that tab, sort and search-form links keep `due=`. It also checks the dashboard (including keyword search through bleve), the org view's dropdown, the milestone page (no dropdown, filter ignored) and an unknown value. I checked that the keyword assertion catches a missing re-index: with the `UpdateIssueIndexer` call removed, it fails. |

## CI / manual verification

Locally, all passing:

```sh
go test ./models/issues/ ./routers/web/user/ ./routers/web/repo/ ./routers/web/shared/... ./services/issue/ ./modules/indexer/issues/...
make 'test-integration#TestIssueDueDateFilter'
go test -run '^(TestAPIIssue|TestAPIEditPull|TestEditIssue|TestIssueDueDate.*|TestMilestone.*|TestNoLoginViewIssues|TestSearchIssues.*|TestUpdateIssueDeadline|TestViewIssues.*|TestPullListGroupByLabelScope|TestRepoProjectFilterByMilestone|TestOrgProjectFilterByMilestone|TestAPIIssuesMilestone)$' gitea.dev/tests/integration
make fmt, make lint-templates, golangci-lint on the changed packages, ./.claude-students/check.sh
```

`make lint-go` reports one pre-existing error in `modules/options/options_bindata.go` (no generated `bindata.dat` locally). The changed packages lint with 0 issues.

I also ran a built binary against a copy of my dev data and checked it by hand:
- Every option on a repo Issues list, with issues overdue, due today, due Thursday and undated, returned the expected rows and Open counts.
- The dashboard `/issues`, including `?q=due&due=today` right after changing a due date, did the same.
- The dropdown's links kept `sort` and `state`.
- The milestone page showed no dropdown and ignored `?due=none`.

## Design

See the Design Decision in #34:
- **Decision 1:** plain deadline bounds rather than a named filter.
- **Decision 2:** a Monday-to-Sunday week.

One consequence to know when reviewing: on the Closed and All tabs, a closed issue matches Overdue by its due date alone, even if it was closed on time.

## AI assistance

Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5) explored the issue-list, dashboard and indexer code paths, drafted the implementation and tests following the existing `UpdatedAfterUnix`/`UpdatedBeforeUnix` and group-by patterns, ran the test suites, and checked the pages in a local instance. I chose the scope and semantics (which pages, pure ranges, Monday-to-Sunday week, re-indexing), reviewed every line, and can explain each change. 1	Suggested new title: Filter issues and pull requests by due date
````
```text
2
3	## User Story
4	As a maintainer running a sprint, I want to filter the issue and pull request lists down to what is overdue, due today, due this week or due soon so that I can triage deadline risk without reading every row.
5
6	## User Scenario
7	A maintainer opens the Issues tab of a repository with 400 open issues. Next to the Labels, Milestones, Projects, Poster and Assignee dropdowns there is a new **Due date** dropdown. They pick **Overdue**. The list now shows only the six issues whose due date has passed, each with its red "Overdue" badge, and the Open/Closed counts above the list say 6 / 0. The URL now ends in `?due=overdue`, so they paste it into the team chat. Later they switch to **Due this week** to plan the next few days, then type a keyword into the search box: the due-date filter stays applied. The same dropdown is on their dashboard Issues and Pull Requests pages (`/issues`, `/pulls`), so they can do the same across all of their repositories.
8
9	## Acceptance Criteria
10	- [ ] AC1: Given a repository's Issues or Pull Requests list, or the dashboard Issues or Pull Requests page (including its organization view), when the page loads, then a **Due date** dropdown is shown with the options All due dates, Overdue, Due today, Due this week, Due soon, Has a due date and No due date. The single-milestone issue page does not show it.
11	- [ ] AC2: Given issues with past, future and no due dates, when **Overdue** (`?due=overdue`) is selected, then only items whose due date is at or before now are listed, and an item with no due date never appears under any option except **No due date**.
12	- [ ] AC3: Given the server UI timezone, when **Due today** is selected, then only items due on today's calendar date are listed. When **Due this week** is selected, only items due between Monday 00:00 and Sunday 23:59:59 of the current week are listed. When **Due soon** is selected, only items due after now and within the same window as the "Due soon" badge (`NearDueDuration`, 72h) are listed, so every open row shows the "Due soon" badge.
13	- [ ] AC4: When **Has a due date** is selected, only items with a due date are listed. When **No due date** is selected, only items without one are listed. Together the two options cover the unfiltered list exactly.
14	- [ ] AC5: Given a selected due-date option, then the Open/Closed counts and the pagination reflect the filter, and the state tabs, search box, other filter dropdowns and page links keep `due=` in their URLs. The filter combines with state, labels, milestone, project, assignee, poster and keyword search.
15	- [ ] AC6: Given an issue whose due date was just changed, when the dashboard is searched with a keyword and a due-date option, then the result uses the new due date.
16	- [ ] AC7: Given an unknown value such as `?due=bogus`, when the page loads, then the list is unfiltered and no error is shown.
17
18	## Out of Scope
19	- The single-milestone issue page, the `/issues/search` JSON endpoints and the REST API (`/api/v1/.../issues`).
20	- Custom date ranges ("due between X and Y") and a configurable first day of the week.
21	- Filtering by the milestone's due date; only the issue's own due date is used.
22	- Changing how the overdue / due-soon badge itself is calculated.
23	- Translations other than en-US (handled by the project's translation process).
24
25	## Open Questions
26	- None.
27
28	## Design Decision
29
30	### Decision 1
31	**Decision:** Translate `?due=` once, in a shared route-level parser, into plain deadline bounds (`DeadlineAfterUnix`, `DeadlineBeforeUnix`, `HasDeadline`) on `IssuesOptions` and the issue indexer's `SearchOptions`, next to the existing `UpdatedAfterUnix` / `UpdatedBeforeUnix` pair.
32	**Alternatives Considered:** (a) A named filter (`overdue`, `soon`, ...) passed down to the model, whose SQL reproduces the badge's open/closed rules (a closed issue is overdue only if it was closed after its deadline). (b) Filtering rows in the browser after the page loads.
33	**Rationale:** Plain ranges work the same in the database and in every search backend (bleve, Elasticsearch, Meilisearch), which the dashboard relies on for keyword searches. Option (a) needs a `closed_unix` against `deadline_unix` comparison that the search backends cannot express. Option (b) breaks counts and pagination. One parser means one clock: "now" comes from `timeutil.TimeStampNow()`, the same clock the badge uses. "Due soon" reuses `NearDueDuration`, so on the Open tab the filter and the badge always agree.
34	**Consequences:** On the Closed and All tabs, a closed issue matches **Overdue** by its deadline alone, even if it was closed on time and so shows no Overdue badge. Every bound also forces `deadline_unix != 0`, so items with no due date can never leak into Overdue; "No due date" matches both 0 and NULL, because the column has no default and some rows hold NULL. Meilisearch needs `deadline_unix` made filterable, which bumps its index version (a one-time re-index on upgrade). Changing an issue's due date now re-indexes it, otherwise a keyword search would filter on the old date.
35
36	### Decision 2
37	**Decision:** "Due this week" is the calendar week, Monday 00:00 to Sunday 23:59:59, in the server UI timezone (`[time] DEFAULT_UI_LOCATION`), the same timezone due dates are saved in.
38	**Alternatives Considered:** A rolling 7 days (today through today+6); a Sunday-to-Saturday week.
39	**Rationale:** It matches the label literally, follows ISO 8601 (Gitea has no week-start setting), and stays clearly different from "Due soon", which is already a rolling 72 hours.
40	**Consequences:** Late in the week the option looks only a few days ahead, and it includes items that went overdue earlier in the same week. Sunday-first users see a Monday-first week.
41
42	## Scope
43	medium (`scope: medium`). One set of query options, one parser and one dropdown shared by four pages. No schema change, since `deadline_unix` already exists and is indexed. The search-backend support and re-index on due-date change add some work.
44
```

```markdown
## User Story
As a maintainer running a sprint, I want to filter the issue and pull request lists down to what is overdue, due today, due this week or due soon so that I can triage deadline risk without reading every row.

## User Scenario
A maintainer opens the Issues tab of a repository with 400 open issues. Next to the Labels, Milestones, Projects, Poster and Assignee dropdowns there is a new **Due date** dropdown. They pick **Overdue**. The list now shows only the six issues whose due date has passed, each with its red "Overdue" badge, and the Open/Closed counts above the list say 6 / 0. The URL now ends in `?due=overdue`, so they paste it into the team chat. Later they switch to **Due this week** to plan the next few days, then type a keyword into the search box: the due-date filter stays applied. The same dropdown is on their dashboard Issues and Pull Requests pages (`/issues`, `/pulls`), so they can do the same across all of their repositories.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given a repository's Issues or Pull Requests list, or the dashboard Issues or Pull Requests page (including its organization view), when the page loads, then a **Due date** dropdown is shown with the options All due dates, Overdue, Due today, Due this week, Due soon, Has a due date and No due date. The single-milestone issue page does not show it.
- [ ] AC2: Given issues with past, future and no due dates, when **Overdue** (`?due=overdue`) is selected, then only items whose due date is at or before now are listed, and an item with no due date never appears under any option except **No due date**.
- [ ] AC3: Given the server UI timezone, when **Due today** is selected, then only items due on today's calendar date are listed. When **Due this week** is selected, only items due between Monday 00:00 and Sunday 23:59:59 of the current week are listed. When **Due soon** is selected, only items due after now and within the same window as the "Due soon" badge (`NearDueDuration`, 72h) are listed, so every open row shows the "Due soon" badge.
- [ ] AC4: When **Has a due date** is selected, only items with a due date are listed. When **No due date** is selected, only items without one are listed. Together the two options cover the unfiltered list exactly.
- [ ] AC5: Given a selected due-date option, then the Open/Closed counts and the pagination reflect the filter, and the state tabs, search box, other filter dropdowns and page links keep `due=` in their URLs. The filter combines with state, labels, milestone, project, assignee, poster and keyword search.
- [ ] AC6: Given an issue whose due date was just changed, when the dashboard is searched with a keyword and a due-date option, then the result uses the new due date.
- [ ] AC7: Given an unknown value such as `?due=bogus`, when the page loads, then the list is unfiltered and no error is shown.

## Out of Scope
- The single-milestone issue page, the `/issues/search` JSON endpoints and the REST API (`/api/v1/.../issues`).
- Custom date ranges ("due between X and Y") and a configurable first day of the week.
- Filtering by the milestone's due date; only the issue's own due date is used.
- Changing how the overdue / due-soon badge itself is calculated.
- Translations other than en-US (handled by the project's translation process).

## Open Questions
- None.

## Design Decision

### Decision 1
**Decision:** Translate `?due=` once, in a shared route-level parser, into plain deadline bounds (`DeadlineAfterUnix`, `DeadlineBeforeUnix`, `HasDeadline`) on `IssuesOptions` and the issue indexer's `SearchOptions`, next to the existing `UpdatedAfterUnix` / `UpdatedBeforeUnix` pair.
**Alternatives Considered:** (a) A named filter (`overdue`, `soon`, ...) passed down to the model, whose SQL reproduces the badge's open/closed rules (a closed issue is overdue only if it was closed after its deadline). (b) Filtering rows in the browser after the page loads.
**Rationale:** Plain ranges work the same in the database and in every search backend (bleve, Elasticsearch, Meilisearch), which the dashboard relies on for keyword searches. Option (a) needs a `closed_unix` against `deadline_unix` comparison that the search backends cannot express. Option (b) breaks counts and pagination. One parser means one clock: "now" comes from `timeutil.TimeStampNow()`, the same clock the badge uses. "Due soon" reuses `NearDueDuration`, so on the Open tab the filter and the badge always agree.
**Consequences:** On the Closed and All tabs, a closed issue matches **Overdue** by its deadline alone, even if it was closed on time and so shows no Overdue badge. Every bound also forces `deadline_unix != 0`, so items with no due date can never leak into Overdue; "No due date" matches both 0 and NULL, because the column has no default and some rows hold NULL. Meilisearch needs `deadline_unix` made filterable, which bumps its index version (a one-time re-index on upgrade). Changing an issue's due date now re-indexes it, otherwise a keyword search would filter on the old date.

### Decision 2
**Decision:** "Due this week" is the calendar week, Monday 00:00 to Sunday 23:59:59, in the server UI timezone (`[time] DEFAULT_UI_LOCATION`), the same timezone due dates are saved in.
**Alternatives Considered:** A rolling 7 days (today through today+6); a Sunday-to-Saturday week.
**Rationale:** It matches the label literally, follows ISO 8601 (Gitea has no week-start setting), and stays clearly different from "Due soon", which is already a rolling 72 hours.
**Consequences:** Late in the week the option looks only a few days ahead, and it includes items that went overdue earlier in the same week. Sunday-first users see a Monday-first week.

## Scope
medium (`scope: medium`). One set of query options, one parser and one dropdown shared by four pages. No schema change, since `deadline_unix` already exists and is indexed. The search-backend support and re-index on due-date change add some work.
```
